variants_and_edge_cases: Game-overtime versus series-overtime: KXNBASERIESOT counts across a playoff series and has a different process (sum of per-game OT indicators with dependency) from a single-game indicator.
Bench definition: points by players who did not start; if a rested starter is replaced, his replacement becomes a starter and leaves the bench count, so lineup changes move the target mechanically.
Overtime inclusion for bench and team-stat targets: OT adds roughly 5 minutes for both teams and about 25 bench minutes in total, and whether OT stats count is not stated.

Multiple overtimes: a game that ends after a second OT satisfies an 'at least 1' indicator but changes team-stat totals more; the OT-count distribution matters for strike markets on totals within this family.
Team-stat head-to-head (team A threes versus team B threes) needs a tie rule (equal counts) that is unseen.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box score and play-by-play: period count for overtime, player starter flags and points for bench scoring, team totals for head-to-head stats.

mechanism.summary: Overtime is the event that regulation margin equals zero, so its probability is the probability mass of the end-of-regulation margin distribution at a single integer. With margin approximately normal with mean mu (the spread) and sd sigma near 12, that mass is phi(mu/sigma)/sigma, about 3.3% at a pick-em, falling to about 2.3% at a 10-point spread and below 1.5% at 14; the observed overall rate is higher, near 6%, because end-of-game strategy (tie-seeking threes, intentional fouling and clock management) piles extra probability at zero and small margins. So P(OT) is strongly decreasing in |spread|, not flat, and is higher for slow, low-variance games. Bench-points markets are different: the outcome is the sum of points from non-starters, a function of how many minutes the bench plays (240 minus starter minutes, plus 25 in OT), the bench's points per minute, and the official starter list that defines who counts. Team-stat head-to-heads compare two correlated counts (the pace shared by both teams creates positive correlation), so the sign and size of the difference depend on volumes and rates, not on a margin tie mass.

stages.name: Regulation margin density at zero
stages.description: P(OT) equals the probability that the regulation margin lands on 0. With the mean set by availability-adjusted ratings and the sd set by pace and the favourite's size, the Gaussian body gives the baseline mass at zero, and that mass shrinks roughly like exp(-mu^2 / (2 sigma^2)); a 12-point favourite is about 40% less likely to need overtime than a pick-em. Slow, low-total games have smaller sigma and so slightly more mass at zero.
stages.distribution: Single-integer mass of a near-normal density, about 3.3% at a pick-em from the Gaussian alone; heteroscedastic in pace; empirical excess to about 6% overall from late-game structure.

stages.name: Late-game tie-forcing strategy
stages.description: In the last minute, the trailing team down by three can attempt a tying three, the leading team can foul to prevent it or defend the three, and clock management determines possessions left. Intentional fouling turns near-ties into free-throw sequences whose outcomes concentrate at margins of 1-4 points. This end-of-game structure puts probability exactly on zero that a smooth margin model misses, and the amount depends on coach policy, free-throw shooting of the ball handlers and whether the team leads by 3.
stages.distribution: Excess point mass at 0 and at +/-1 to 3 compared to a Gaussian; amount is policy-dependent and not captured by ratings.

stages.name: Overtime length and what it adds
stages.description: Given overtime, the game adds one five-minute period (about 22-26 total points) with a second OT in a minority of overtime games, adding 25 bench-plus-starter minutes per period to both teams. Starters play heavy minutes in OT with bench usage low unless fouls intervene, so OT changes the minute split between starters and bench and the team stat counts for head-to-head markets.
stages.distribution: Number of OT periods: geometric-like with P(second OT | first OT) about 0.07-0.10; points in OT approximately normal with sd 7-8.

stages.name: Bench minutes and bench scoring rate
stages.description: Bench points = bench minutes times bench points per minute. Bench minutes are what is left after the starters' minutes, which fall in blowouts and when foul trouble hits, and rise when a starter is out and the bench is deep. The points per minute reflect bench scorers' usage, which depends on whether a sixth man is a primary scorer and on the second unit's lineup. The definition of bench via the starter list moves the target when a starter is rested.
stages.distribution: Bench points have sd about 8 around means of about 35 points; strongly state-dependent (blowout state shifts bench minutes by 20+). Non-negative, right-skewed.

stages.name: Team-stat pair distribution
stages.description: Team A stat minus Team B stat (for instance three-pointers made) has mean from volume and rate differences and a variance that depends on both teams' attempts; the two counts are positively correlated through game pace and negatively through score-state effects, so the difference is narrower than independent counts. Strikes at zero need a tie rule, and a team that trails takes more threes late, changing the volume.
stages.distribution: Difference of two overdispersed counts with correlation about +0.2 to 0.3 from shared pace; discrete with a mass at zero.

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from nba.margin sd model (about 12, scale sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.why: Overtime is the whole contract in KXNBAOT and the density-at-zero formulation gives the correct dependence on spread and pace.

nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.label: Coach-level tie-forcing and intentional-foul policy
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.mechanism: How often a team trailing by 2-3 in the last 30 seconds attempts a tying three or a fast two, and how often the leading team fouls up three.
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.rationale: Excess tie mass comes from end-of-game choices; teams differ, and the same game state yields a tie more often when the trailing coach shoots for the tie than when he fouls and hopes.
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.measurement: From play-by-play: in games within 3 points with <30 seconds left, share of trailing-team possessions ending in a 3PA, a 2PA or a foul-drawn FT; leading-team foul-up-3 rate; compute per coach over 3 seasons (min 15 events) with shrinkage k=10 events to league mean; produce per-matchup tie-conditional probability = P(close at 30s) × P(tie | close, policies).
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.why: Gives the excess zero mass a coach-level driver.

nba.ot_period_distribution.label: Distribution of number of overtime periods and OT scoring
nba.ot_period_distribution.mechanism: If overtime occurs, additional periods occur with a small probability and each period adds a fixed block of minutes and points.
nba.ot_period_distribution.rationale: The count of OT periods matters for series OT markets and for strike markets on total, bench or team stats within the family; the draft treats OT as one event.
nba.ot_period_distribution.measurement: Empirical P(k OT periods) from 15 seasons: P(1), P(2), P(3+) conditional on OT; per-period points per team sampled from the league distribution adjusted for pace (mean about 11-12 per team per 5 minutes, sd 5); update yearly; for series OT use sum of independent Bernoulli(P(OT)) with series-level sd inflation.
nba.ot_period_distribution.why: Distinguishes first from second OT where strikes differ, and supports series-level OT counts.

nba.bench_minutes_distribution.label: Bench minutes distribution (240 + 25k minus starter minutes)
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.mechanism: Bench points depend on bench minutes first; they equal total team minutes minus starter minutes and shrink when starters play heavy minutes in close games or OT.
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.rationale: The draft's bench input is points share, while the better predictor is minutes times points per minute with a state-dependent minutes distribution.
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.measurement: Per team: bench minutes = 240 + 25*OT - Σ starter minutes; model starter minutes as scenario mixture (blowout/close/OT/foul trouble) with weights from own-model margin; bench points = bench minutes × bench points-per-minute with 30-game half-life and shrinkage k=300 minutes; as-of lineups; output mean/sd by scenario.
free_sources: nba_api box score minutes and starters
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.why: A bench-points strike is a minutes question first; blowout and OT regimes shift it by 15-25 minutes.

nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.label: Starter/bench designation ledger and rest-driven reclassification
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.mechanism: The bench is the set of players not in the official starting five, so a starter absence promotes the next man into the starter group and shifts scoring from bench to starter.
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.rationale: The draft interaction says a rested starter becomes a bench player, but a rested starter does not play; the real effects are (a) a promoted bench player moves out of the bench count and (b) a returning star on a restriction coming off the bench moves in.
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.measurement: Record for each team-game: official starters list, status of expected starters, bench designation of the primary scorers; compute counterfactual bench points under tonight's starter list using player points-per-minute and projected minutes: bench_pts = Σ_{non-starters} proj_min × ppm; adjust for returning player minute limits; as-of lineup confirmation.
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.why: The market's definition of bench changes with the starter list so the estimate must be conditional on the list.

nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.label: Team-stat pair difference model (shared-pace correlation)
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.mechanism: The head-to-head team stat is the difference of two counts with positive correlation through game pace and negative through script effects.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.rationale: Treating the two teams' counts as independent overstates the sd of the difference and misprices the zero-tie mass.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.measurement: For team stat X (e.g. 3PM): mean_X = attempts_X × rate_X using opponent-adjusted rates (20-game half-life, k=150 attempts); sd_diff from joint empirical covariance over 3 seasons: var = var_A + var_B - 2 rho sd_A sd_B with rho from pace; compute P(A>B), P(tie) with discrete negative binomial convolution; blowout correction increasing trailing-team attempts.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.why: Team-stat markets inside this family use a different distribution from the tie-mass logic of OT.

nba.ot_model.reason: Right target but described as an empirical frequency by spread and total bucket; a bucketed frequency from market lines is partly circular and ignores the Gaussian density structure supplied by reg_tie_pmf_model.

nba.score_resid.reason: Margin density near zero is the central object, but the residual distribution must be built from own-model predictions rather than lines.

nba.garbage.reason: Captures blowout shifts of bench minutes and lower tie mass, but it is the same information as the spread effect on P(OT) and only separately useful for bench points.

nba.bench_scoring.reason: Bench points per minute and depth is the second factor of the bench target, but without bench minutes it explains little.

nba.starters_pit.reason: Defines who counts as bench; essential, but the timing of confirmation and the promoted-player effect must be explicit.

nba.rotation.reason: Substitution patterns by margin decide bench minutes; needs per-coach estimates and margin-conditional minute curves.

nba.pace.reason: Pace scales sd of margin (tie mass) and team-stat counts; it is a main driver for the pair model but minor for bench minutes.

nba.q_scoring.reason: Quarter/half scoring patterns pertain to period markets, which are not in this archetype; no OT, bench or team-stat target uses them.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Relevant to the excess tie mass but too generic; the coach-level tie-forcing rate and foul-up-3 policy are needed to make it measurable.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Starter absences set both the margin mean and the bench composition; vintage matters because replacements are only known near tip.

nba.off_rtg.reason: Draft rationale mentions race-to markets that are not in this archetype; ratings matter only to set the mean margin and scoring volumes.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Same issue as off_rtg: the rationale refers to race-to markets; defence determines mean margin only and affects tie mass weakly.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: Claimed to drive OT frequency, but shooting luck is unpredictable and does not forecast ties; it is useful only for team three-point head-to-heads.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the overtime and team-event markets; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook price for the overtime and team-event markets is a market-derived quantity; keep as a comparison benchmark to measure disagreement, do not use as an input to the probability model.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule converts a probability gap into net edge for the overtime and team-event markets; needed for decision thresholds only, constant with respect to the outcome.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Low-probability OT contracts are exactly where favourite-longshot bias could exist; as a post-model calibration layer, it is only meaningful after enough settled OT markets exist.

interactions.mechanism: The tie probability is the Gaussian pmf at zero, which decays like exp(-mu^2/(2 sigma^2)); the loss from a 4-point spread to a 10-point spread is far larger than from 0 to 4, so the effect of spread on P(OT) is convex-then-flat in the tail.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin games by own-model spread (0-2, 2-5, 5-8, 8-12, 12+) and compare the observed OT rate with the Gaussian prediction and with a flat rate.

interactions.mechanism: The excess tie mass is conditional on the game being within three points with under 30 seconds left and on the trailing coach's policy; if the leading team intentionally fouls, ties become less likely than by smooth density.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(tie | within 3 at 0:30) by coach pair and contrast with fouling versus non-fouling policies.

interactions.mechanism: When the top scorer is promoted into the starting five by an absence, he leaves the bench count and bench points drop by his share; when a returning star plays off the bench on a restriction, bench points rise by his minutes times his rate, a discrete jump.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare bench points in games with promoted-starter and with star-off-bench changes versus baselines.

interactions.mechanism: Bench minutes rise with blowout probability but saturate once starters sit entirely, around 150-170 minutes; beyond that extra blowout size adds nothing, while within the competitive range additional margin adds quickly.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot bench minutes against final margin to find the saturation; fit a piecewise-linear spline.

interactions.mechanism: The two teams' counts rise and fall together with pace, so a pace shock moves both and leaves the difference nearly unchanged; the difference's sd is smaller than independent counts would give, and the covariance is higher in games with competitive scores.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate rho of team threes by pace tercile and by closeness of final score.

nonlinearities.shape: Gaussian bell in the spread with an empirical multiplicative excess
nonlinearities.why: P(OT) falls as exp(-(spread/sigma)^2/2), so it declines by about 30% at a 10-point spread, and the excess factor lifts all levels by about 1.7-1.9.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: flat in close games, rising then saturating in blowouts
nonlinearities.why: Bench minutes are about 90-100 when close, grow rapidly when margin exceeds 15, and cap near the whole-bench total once starters sit.

nonlinearities.shape: Geometric decay in number of OT periods
nonlinearities.why: Each extra overtime period occurs with a small probability that is roughly constant, so tail periods add little mass and multi-OT strike markets are rare events with unstable estimates.

contract.settlement_definition: The sampled full-game total (KXNBATOTAL) settles Yes if the combined points in the named game exceed a half-point strike (floor_strike 274.5 for 'over 274.5 total points'), so no push is possible; the secondary text settles on the official final result for a game that starts within 48 hours of schedule and resolves to a fair price if the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours. The wording says 'total points scored in the game' without carving out overtime, so overtime is counted by default but is not explicitly stated. KXNBASUMMERTOTAL (Summer League) and KXNBASERIESGAMES (series total games, a count of games not points) have no sampled rules and are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: If over 274.5 total points are scored in the Washington vs Atlanta Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike is a half-point 'over' on combined team points in one named game, so the target is a continuous-looking integer sum with no push.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time
rules_evidence.establishes: A short postponement does not void the market: it resolves on the official final result, whereas a longer delay or cancellation resolves to fair price (void-like), so postponement risk is not a loss.

variants_and_edge_cases: Regular-season total (KXNBATOTAL), Summer League total (KXNBASUMMERTOTAL) and series games total (KXNBASERIESGAMES) share a label but have different generating processes; the third counts games in a series, not points.

Overtime: the rule text says 'total points scored in the game'; a game with one overtime adds about 24 points, so P(over) near the line rises materially when OT is included; inclusion is plausible but not stated.
Strike spacing: rungs are half-point lines, and the ladder is a survival function of a discrete integer sum, so adjacent rungs differ by P(total = k).
Postponement and cancellation: a cancelled or non-started game resolves to fair price rather than No, which affects only edge accounting.
Summer League rosters, minutes and pace are not NBA rotation; the total there has a larger dependence on minute plans and a different sd.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final score of the game (league box score), including overtime unless the full rule text excludes it.

mechanism.summary: A game total is points = possessions times combined points per possession, so the process has two multiplicative factors and one additive tail. Possessions come from the interaction of two teams' preferred tempos (pace is neither the average nor the slower team's pace, it depends on transition frequency, turnovers and who pushes after makes or misses), reduced by dead-ball time from fouls and free throws. Points per possession depend on each offence against the other's defence for the actual rotation, including who is out (a missing ball handler slows pace and lowers efficiency, a missing rim protector raises efficiency without changing pace), plus free-throw volume driven by foul rates and the officials. Three-point shooting variance is the dominant noise source so the game-level sd of about 17-19 points is heteroscedastic: higher for teams that attempt many threes. Close games add late-game fouling free throws, blowouts shorten starters' minutes, and overtime adds about 24 points in about 6% of games. The settled event is one integer sum against a half-point strike.

stages.name: Possession count from two tempos
stages.description: Game possessions are not the average of the teams' season paces; they depend on offensive transition rate, turnover and steal rates, missed-shot rebound speed and the opponent's own tempo response, plus dead-ball events (fouls, timeouts). A slow, half-court team can slow a fast opponent, but evidence that the slower team fully controls pace is mixed, so the composition rule must be estimated rather than assumed. Pace has a game-to-game sd of about 3 possessions.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal with sd of 3-4 possessions around the composed mean, with weak dependence on the game state (garbage time slightly slower or faster depending on bench).

stages.name: Active-set efficiency of both offences
stages.description: Each offence's points per possession depends on shot quality against the specific defence and on who plays; absences affect pace and efficiency differently by role (a lead ball handler out lowers assist-generated shots and pace, a rim protector out raises the opponent's rim efficiency). The relevant baseline is opponent-adjusted offence and defence separately, not net rating, because a total depends on the sum of both teams' offences rather than their difference.
stages.distribution: Normal with sd about 1.5-2.5 points per 100 possessions around the estimated rating; scenario mixture when key players are questionable.

stages.name: Shot-making noise and its volume dependence
stages.description: Game-level variance is dominated by three-point makes: each three has Bernoulli variance 9p(1-p), so a team taking 45 threes contributes much more variance than one taking 25, and the variance of the total rises with both teams' 3PA. Hot shooting regresses to talent and shot quality, so recent results must be shrunk, and the shrinkage is stronger for defences' opponent 3P%.
stages.distribution: Sum of Bernoulli/binomial shot outcomes: total sd roughly sqrt(var of 2s + var of 3s + var of FT) of about 14, plus possession and rating uncertainty giving 17-19; heteroscedastic in 3PA.

stages.name: Free-throw volume and late-game structure
stages.description: Free throws add points through foul rates (offensive drive rate, defensive contact), the officiating crew's whistle tendency and late-game fouling in close games. When the margin is within about 8 points in the last two minutes, the trailing team fouls and total points rise by 4-10; in blowouts the late phase has no intentional fouls and benches play, which reduces scoring pace for some teams and increases it for others.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed in close games (extra FT tail), compressed in blowouts; crew effect about +/-3 points in total at the extremes.

stages.name: Overtime and series-length variants
stages.description: With about 6% probability the game adds an overtime period, whose combined points have mean about 23-25 and sd about 8, pushing the total over most lines near the median; a strict over for P=0.5 near the line gains about 3 percentage points from OT. The series-games contract is not a points process at all: it counts games from a best-of-seven, requiring per-game win probabilities, home-court pattern and between-game dependence.
stages.distribution: Mixture: regulation sum plus Bernoulli(0.06) OT block; series length is a discrete {4,5,6,7} distribution derived from game win probabilities.

nba.game_pace_composition.label: Game-pace composition rule from two teams' tempos
nba.game_pace_composition.mechanism: Expected game possessions as a function of both teams' pace, transition frequency and turnover rates rather than a simple average.
nba.game_pace_composition.rationale: The draft states that the slower team controls tempo; the empirical rule must be fitted, with transition frequency and defence-forced turnovers as additional terms.
nba.game_pace_composition.measurement: Regress game possessions on (paceA + paceB)/2, |paceA - paceB|, each team's transition-frequency and turnover rate and rest, using 5 seasons of team-games with opponent-adjusted paces (20-game half-life); report coefficients and residual sd; as-of the last completed game; adjust for active set via nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decomposition.
nba.game_pace_composition.why: Total is multiplicative in possessions, so a 2-possession error shifts the mean total by about 4 points.

nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.label: Absence effect split into pace and efficiency components
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.mechanism: Each rotation player's absence changes team pace and ORtg/DRtg separately, with different signs by role.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.rationale: The existing lineup_adj_rating collapses availability into one net rating, which is the right variable for margin but wrong for totals where a slower-and-worse offence and a faster-and-weaker defence have opposite effects.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.measurement: For each player with at least 800 minutes: on/off differences in team possessions per 48, ORtg and DRtg over 3 seasons with ridge shrinkage (k=600 possessions) and teammate adjustment (RAPM-style regression on pace as well); apply to tonight's scenario weights; as-of nightly after injury report.
raw_data: lineup stints with possessions and points
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.why: The draft's interaction about ball handlers and rim protectors has no measurable input behind it.

nba.three_point_variance_load.label: Three-point attempt volume as a variance load
nba.three_point_variance_load.mechanism: The sd of the total depends on how many threes both teams attempt and on the dispersion of free-throw and two-point results.
nba.three_point_variance_load.rationale: The draft says total sd is about 17-19 as a constant; it varies with shot mix, and wide-open three-heavy teams produce a wider total distribution that matters at ladder tails.
nba.three_point_variance_load.measurement: Var_total = Σ_team [9*3PA*p3(1-p3) + 4*2PA*p2(1-p2) + FTA*pft(1-pft)] + var(possessions)*ppp^2*... using opponent-adjusted attempts and rates (20-game half-life); calibrate a scale factor lambda so that predicted variance matches realised total residual variance in 2 prior seasons; report sd per game and skew.
nba.three_point_variance_load.why: Ladder rungs far from the mean depend on the tail; using a constant sd misprices those rungs.

nba.series_length_distribution.label: Series-length distribution from per-game win probabilities
nba.series_length_distribution.mechanism: The number of games in a best-of-seven series is a function of per-game win probability, home pattern and dependence between games.
nba.series_length_distribution.rationale: KXNBASERIESGAMES counts games, not points; the draft has no input for it except a generic series model reference outside the archetype.
nba.series_length_distribution.measurement: P(series ends in k games) by dynamic programming over home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 with per-game win probabilities from own-model ratings and series dependence parameter (game-to-game correlation about +0.05 on margin, estimated from 2000-2025 playoff series); injuries known as of the as-of date; output P(4), P(5), P(6), P(7).
nba.series_length_distribution.why: Series-length markets have a separate target requiring a binomial-type calculation.

interactions.mechanism: Total equals possessions times combined points per possession, so a fast game between two efficient offences is multiplicatively larger than the sum of separate pace and efficiency effects; the cross term is about 1.5-2 points when both factors are one sd above average.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress total on pace, efficiency and the pace-by-efficiency product across 5 seasons and test the product term.

interactions.mechanism: Missing a primary ball handler lowers pace and efficiency (total falls), while missing a rim protector raises opponent efficiency without changing pace (total rises); the sign depends on the missing role.
interactions.how_to_test: Group games by missing player role and compare residual totals; verify opposite signs.

interactions.mechanism: Crew whistle tendency matters most for teams that live at the line: a high-foul crew adds free-throw points proportional to both teams' free-throw rate, so the crew effect on total is larger when both offences draw many fouls.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact crew foul index with the sum of both teams' FTA rate and test the slope.

interactions.mechanism: A hot three-point streak is more likely to be luck for a high-3PA team (larger noise per game), so regression is heavier for those teams and the variance load is also larger; direction: shrink recent offence more when volume is high.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress next-game total residual on last-10 3P% residual interacted with 3PA rate.

interactions.mechanism: Close games produce both late-fouling free-throw points and OT, so the extra points are positively correlated within the same games; the upper tail of the total is generated by close games more than by high-pace blowouts.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition total residuals on final margin buckets and compare tail mass of high rungs in close vs non-close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance increasing in 3PA, sd scales with sqrt(attempts)
nonlinearities.why: The sd of the total rises with the number of threes (9p(1-p) per attempt), so rung probabilities away from the mean are sensitive to shot mix.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at margin within about 8 points in the last 2 minutes
nonlinearities.why: Intentional fouling begins when a game is within a possession or two; adds 4-10 points only in that state, a switch rather than a slope in the margin.

nonlinearities.shape: Mixture adding a fixed block to the upper tail
nonlinearities.why: The regulation total plus a 24-point OT block in 6% of games creates a bump to the right of the median that a normal misses.

nonlinearities.shape: Sub-linear in the slower team's pace
nonlinearities.why: If the slow team partially controls tempo, game pace responds less than one-for-one to the faster team's tempo, so the average of paces overstates the effect of the fast side.

contract.settlement_definition: No live series is filed under this archetype key in the ledger; the live win-margin series KXNBAWINMARGIN is filed under game_moneyline_spread, and its sampled rule asks whether a named team wins the game 'by 6 to 10 points', settled on the official final result including overtime, with a fair-price void if the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours. Band edges beyond the one sampled band (1-5, 11-15, 16+), the treatment of the other team winning, and whether each band is a separate market per side are not verified under this key.
variants_and_edge_cases: Per-side bands: the sampled market names the winning team (Brooklyn by 6 to 10), so each game has a set of mutually exclusive bands for each side whose probabilities must sum to one across both sides.
Closed integer bands (6 to 10 inclusive) mean margins of 5 and 11 fall outside; with NBA integer scores no push or gap exists between adjacent bands.
Overtime converts every regulation tie into a final margin of typically 1-8 points, adding mass to the lowest band beyond what a smooth density gives.
Postponement within 48 hours still settles on the official final result; beyond that the market voids at fair price.
Whether the highest band is open-ended (16+ or 21+) is unseen; its mass depends on the heavy tail of blowouts.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final score of the game, overtime included.

mechanism.summary: A winning-margin band is the probability that the final signed margin falls in a closed integer interval on one side, so the contract is a histogram of one density, not a binary on the mean. The density has four structural features beyond a normal with mean mu and sd sigma: a hole at zero (no ties, so regulation ties move to overtime), a bump at small positive margins from overtime outcomes (final margin after OT is typically 1-8), late-game compression when the trailing team fouls and the leading team keeps the lead at small values, and compression after starters are pulled in blowouts where bench units trim or inflate the margin depending on the second unit's strength. The sum across all bands and both sides must be exactly one, and the middle bands are driven by sigma more than by mu; a band such as 6-10 is the difference of two CDF values, so sigma errors enter directly. The informative inputs are therefore the mean margin from the active-set ratings, the heteroscedastic sd and the empirical shape corrections, in that order.

stages.name: Signed-margin mean and variance
stages.description: The mean of the signed margin comes from the difference of the active-set ratings plus home court, and its sd is about 11-13 and rises with pace and with favourite size. The band probabilities are far more sensitive to sd than win probability is: at mean 6 a one-point change in sd moves the 6-10 band by about 2 percentage points, while P(win) changes by less than one. The mean uncertainty from questionable players is a mixture that fattens bands on the underdog side.
stages.distribution: Normal body with sd 11-13, heteroscedastic; scenario mixture over star status gives a bimodal signed-margin density before pooling.

stages.name: Final-minutes compression and parity
stages.description: In the last two minutes the trailing team fouls and the leading team shoots free throws, so margins within about 8 points shift toward specific values (a made three moves a 4-point lead to 7, an intentional foul sequence ends at +2 to +6), and a ten-point-plus lead with a minute left is basically fixed. The pmf therefore has spikes and troughs by parity and key numbers (3, 6) that a smooth density does not reproduce. The strength of this effect depends on how often the game is close in the last minutes.
stages.distribution: Non-smooth pmf over margins 1-12 with parity structure; the spikes are about 10-20% relative deviations from the smooth density.

stages.name: Garbage-time margin decay
stages.description: When the lead is large (+15 or more) late in the fourth quarter, coaches pull starters and the bench trades baskets; the final margin is then the margin at the pull time plus a random walk whose drift depends on the relative quality of the two second units and on how early each coach pulls. Leads typically shrink a few points after starters sit, but a deep bench on the leading side can hold or extend the margin. This sets the shape of the 11-15 versus 16+ bands, not the middle bands.
stages.distribution: Margin after the pull: approximately a random walk with sd about 4 points over 6 minutes and drift of -1 to -3 points; strongly dependent on lead size at the time of the pull.

stages.name: Overtime conversion into low bands
stages.description: If the regulation score ties (about 3% from the smooth density and about 6% empirically) a five-minute period is played and the final margin is the OT margin, with a mean absolute value near 5.5 and nearly all outcomes between 1 and 10. This adds roughly 3 percentage points of mass to the 1-5 bands in total that a continuous density would assign elsewhere, and it matters most for bands near zero when the spread is small.
stages.distribution: Tie mass converted into a folded normal with sd about 7 (five minutes of scoring difference); dependence on |spread| through the tie probability.

stages.name: Band construction and coherence
stages.description: The market lists bands for each side, so the model must produce P(A wins by band b) for all bands and both teams and the sum must be one. Because each band is a difference of the CDF at its edges, the cut points near the median of the margin density are sensitive to bias in mu, while the open-ended top band is sensitive to the tail. Rungs priced independently by the market may violate the sum constraint or the unimodality of the density within a side.
stages.distribution: Multinomial over 8-10 outcomes with a unimodal-per-side density; sum-to-one constraint couples all bands.

opponent_matchup.note: Scheme clash width and second-unit match-up.

role_personnel.note: Who plays after starters sit decides margin decay.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and travel shift the mean margin by about a point, which is carried by the rating and home-court terms in the moneyline archetype; bands add no independent environmental mechanism.

pace_volume.note: Possessions scale the variance of the margin.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting efficiency matters here only through the rating and the variance; luck regression of ratings belongs to the moneyline archetype and has no band-specific extension.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Seeding stakes and rest decide starter minutes in lopsided games and whether coaches pull starters early, but no input links the motivation state to pull timing; blowout probability alone does not capture it.

officiating_rules.note: Referee tendencies shift free-throw counts and the late-game foul sequence only marginally, and no evidence ties crew identity to margin bands beyond what pace and fouls already capture.

nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.label: Empirical final-margin pmf by own-model mean and sd
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.mechanism: The final margin has non-smooth pmf structure (hole at zero, OT bump, late-game parity) that a normal density does not reproduce.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.rationale: The draft names score_resid as the margin density by spread bucket, but spread buckets from market lines are circular and the pmf structure lives at the integer level; band edges at 5/6 and 10/11 fall exactly on such structure.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.measurement: Collect 15 seasons of final signed margins; standardise z = (margin - mu_own)/sigma_own using own-model mean and sd; estimate the pmf of the integer margin by kernel smoothing of the z-density plus an explicit multiplicative correction per integer margin in [-12, 12] (ridge-shrunk to 1); validate by log-loss of band probabilities in 2 held-out seasons; recompute annually.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.why: The market has bands, and the discretisation edges at 5/6, 10/11 coincide with the pmf irregularities.

nba.margin_decay_after_pull.label: Margin decay after starters are pulled (by coach and lead size)
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.mechanism: The final margin equals the margin at the pull time plus a bench-vs-bench drift whose size depends on lead and coach.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.rationale: Blowout probability alone does not tell how much a 20-point lead at 6:00 shrinks; a coach who pulls starters early gives up points.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.measurement: From play-by-play: margin at the time both starters of the leading team are out and the final margin; compute mean and sd of the change by lead bucket (10-14, 15-19, 20+) and by coach with 3 seasons of data, shrunk to league with k=8 games; as-of the last completed game; output drift and sd for tonight's coaches.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.why: 11-15 and 16+ bands depend on the drift after the pull, which no input measures.

nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.label: Second-unit net rating gap
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.mechanism: The bench lineups play most late blowout minutes, so the margin drift is the second unit's net rating difference.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.rationale: Starter-based team ratings say nothing about who wins the last six minutes of a blowout; a deep bench preserves a lead.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.measurement: Net rating of the lineups with at most one top-5 player, per 100 possessions, over the last 40 games with opponent adjustment and shrinkage k=250 possessions; gap = team A second unit minus team B second unit; translate to expected margin drift per 6 minutes = gap × 12/100; as-of rotation as projected.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.why: A blowout winner with a weak bench ends in a lower band than the starters' ratings imply.

nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.label: Final-margin pmf conditional on overtime
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.mechanism: If regulation ties, the final margin is the margin of a five-minute period (or more), concentrated in 1-8 points.
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.rationale: Mass of the lowest bands is the sum of a regulation part and an OT part; the OT part follows a different distribution with folded structure.
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.measurement: Empirical pmf of |final margin| for games with OT_periods = 1, 2, 3+ over 15 seasons; fit folded-normal with sd s_OT estimated by maximum likelihood (about 6-7 for one OT); combine with P(OT) from the tie model: P(band) = P(reg in band)(1-P(OT)) + P(OT) × P(OT margin in band).
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.why: Lowest bands (1-5) get a sizeable share from OT that a Gaussian misses.

nba.score_resid.reason: Described as the empirical margin density by spread bucket, but spread buckets come from market lines (circular) and it is not tied to the integer band edges that settle this contract.

nba.garbage.reason: Probability of a large lead drives the upper bands, but it is a probability of blowout, not the decay of the margin after starters sit.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Provides the mean signed margin; the band is more sensitive to sd than to this mean, so its precision is not the bottleneck.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: A star in or out moves the mean by several points and creates a bimodal density that fattens bands on both sides.

nba.pace.reason: Pace scales sd of margin (more possessions, more variance), which drives middle-band probabilities; effect on mean is nil.

nba.ot_model.reason: Provides P(OT) but not the conversion of OT into final margins, which sets the lowest band masses.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Late fouling shifts the pmf at margins 1-8, a real effect, but the draft states it only qualitatively.

nba.off_rtg.reason: Component of the mean margin; offence and defence differ in variance contribution but this is minor for bands.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Component of the mean margin; redundant with lineup_adj_rating for the mean.

nba.rotation.reason: Marked context in the draft but starter pull timing is what controls the upper bands; mislabelled and should be primary for the 11+ bands.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Claims that scheme clashes widen or narrow the margin, but there is little evidence of variance effects beyond pace; the mean effect is already in ratings.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook price for the winning-margin bands is a market-derived quantity; keep as a comparison benchmark to measure disagreement, do not use as an input to the probability model.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Band prices should sum to one across both sides and be unimodal per side; violations flag stale quotes or arbitrage but come from the market, so they cannot be model inputs.

interactions.mechanism: A band probability is a CDF difference (mu-b)/sigma, so errors in sigma and in mu multiply: when the mean is near a band's centre, sigma matters more than mu, but for a band two sds away mu matters more.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the sensitivity of band probabilities to sigma and mu on a grid and identify where each error dominates.

interactions.mechanism: Once the lead exceeds about 15 with under six minutes left the starters leave and the margin drifts rather than grows; the effect of an extra point of lead on the final margin falls from about one to about 0.5 beyond the threshold.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress final margin on margin at 6:00 with a hinge at 15 and compare slope above and below.

interactions.mechanism: The drift after the pull depends on the second-unit gap: a leading team with the stronger bench keeps its lead, otherwise it shrinks; the sign is conditional on the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Group blowouts by the second-unit gap tercile and compare mean change of margin after pull.

interactions.mechanism: In the regime where regulation ties (3-6% of games) the final margin follows the folded OT density, which is concentrated in 1-8; the lowest bands are a mixture of regulation and OT regimes and the mixture weight falls with spread.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the mixture with mixture weight as a function of own-model spread and compare log loss against a single density.

interactions.mechanism: In a faster game there are more possessions in the final two minutes, so the late-foul sequences take more time and add margins in 4-8 points; pmf spikes become less pronounced as pace rises.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast the final-margin pmf at 1-8 points in the top versus bottom pace tercile in close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Slope falls from 1 to about 0.5 beyond a 15-point lead at 6:00
nonlinearities.why: Coaches pull starters when a lead is large; additional lead points are given back by bench play, so the final margin is a concave function of the late margin.

nonlinearities.shape: Non-smooth with parity spikes and a zero hole
nonlinearities.why: Integer margins show relative deviations from a smooth density by up to 10-20% at margins 1-8, which determine band edges at 5/6 and 10/11.

nonlinearities.shape: Heteroscedastic: sd grows with favourite size and pace
nonlinearities.why: Wider spreads have larger sd (heavy tail of blowouts), so band probabilities on the favourite side spread out more than a constant-sd model implies.

contract.settlement_definition: Each market resolves Yes only if a specific, officially confirmed off-court event occurs inside a stated window, and the sampled rules define the qualifying stage narrowly: a team sale needs the deal 'finalized and approved by the Governing League', a stake sale needs a signed definitive agreement (closing may come later), a franchise-value market needs a definitive purchase agreement plus approvals and a headline value above the strike, a league announcement needs a firm decision naming a confirmed inaugural season, retirement needs an announcement of intent effective immediately or before the next season, and a rule change needs formal adoption before the 2026-27 regular season. Windows are in Eastern Time and end on stated dates; absent the event, all markets resolve No.

rules_evidence.quote: The deal must be finalized and approved by the Governing League to be encompassed by the Payout Criterion.
rules_evidence.establishes: Team-sale Yes requires league approval, not merely an agreement or a report, so the qualifying stage is the end of the governance pipeline.

rules_evidence.quote: Negotiations, letters of intent, drafts, rumors, and unexecuted or conditional announcements do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: A stake-sale Yes needs a signed definitive agreement; the earlier stages that reporters cover are explicitly excluded, so reporter signals are only leading indicators.

rules_evidence.quote: Preliminary discussions, negotiations, statements of general intent, and a possible earliest start without a confirmed inaugural season do not qualify.
rules_evidence.establishes: A league announcement must name a confirmed inaugural season; statements of intent do not count, creating a sharp wording threshold.

rules_evidence.quote: Merely selecting a preferred bidder is insufficient.
rules_evidence.establishes: Franchise-value Yes needs a definitive agreement and approvals with the headline value above the strike, and bundled assets are stripped out.

rules_evidence.quote: The retirement must be intended to be effective immediately or prior to the first new season after the announcement.
rules_evidence.establishes: Retirement markets need an announcement with a timing condition, so a vague 'this will be my last year' statement may not satisfy it.

variants_and_edge_cases: Qualifying stage differs by series: announcement (KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE, KXNBARETIRE), definitive agreement (KXNBASTAKESALE), definitive agreement plus all approvals (KXNBAFRANCHISECOST), finalized and approved (KXNBATEAMSALE), or formal adoption (KXNBARULE).
Windows and time zone: announcements must occur after market issuance and before the stated date in Eastern Time, so an event announced late on the closing date can fall on either side.

Exclusions and carve-outs: 'one free throw' rule excludes the last two minutes of the fourth quarter and overtime, the governor market excludes the holder at issuance and any acting or alternate governor, bundled assets are stripped from headline values.

Multi-outcome construction: Next Team and Next Contract markets have several mutually exclusive outcomes with a catch-all (Retires / No Team), where partial re-signs and extensions do not trigger early resolution.

Fifteen of the 22 live series have no sampled rules (trades, pick trades, apology, executive award, relocation, stadium, expansion, White House attendance and others), so their qualifying stages are unverified.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league or team announcements, league-approved transaction records and credible primary reporting where the rule allows; no single stat feed.

mechanism.summary: Off-court events are sparse, one-off outcomes generated by organisations, so the mechanism is a process of stage-gated progress against a deadline rather than a rate per opportunity. An event happens when (1) it is feasible under league rules and finances (salary cap and apron constraints for trades, board-of-governors approval for sales and relocations, expansion process), (2) a decision-maker with incentives chooses to pursue it (an owner's liquidity and valuation, a front office's competitive position, a player's career horizon), (3) counterparties agree and the process clears its approval stages, each with typical durations, and (4) a qualifying public act occurs inside the window and at the stage the contract wording requires (announcement, signed definitive agreement, completed approval). Information arrives through reporters whose reliability varies by outlet and by stage, so the key variable is not the rumor but the stage reached and the historical time from that stage to the qualifying act. Hazards are not uniform: they spike around calendar landmarks (draft, free agency, trade deadline, Board meetings).

stages.name: Feasibility under league rules and finances
stages.description: Whether an event can happen at all is governed by hard constraints: trade salary matching tied to payroll tiers (the apron levels), roster size, moratorium dates, the league approval requirement for sales and relocation, the expansion process and the CBA rules for contract extensions. An infeasible event has probability near zero regardless of rumors, and a feasible event has a conditional probability given the actors' incentives; the two are multiplied.
stages.distribution: Binary feasibility gate times a continuous incentive term; feasibility is deterministic given payroll and roster data and is often the cleanest source of low probabilities.

stages.name: Actor incentive and hazard rate
stages.description: Given feasibility, the decision-maker's incentive determines the base hazard: a coach on a team far below preseason expectation, an owner facing a large capital need, a veteran player approaching the end of a contract all have elevated hazards. The base hazard is estimated from reference classes (how often coaches are fired in a given record-vs-expectation bucket, how often franchises sell) and then updated by org-specific facts.
stages.distribution: Low-rate hazard process, over-dispersed across organisations; discrete events with heavy clustering around specific calendar points.

stages.name: Deal stage progression and approval pipeline
stages.description: Sales, trades and expansions move through ordered stages (exploration, exclusivity, definitive agreement, governance approval, closing), each with a stage-specific completion probability and a typical delay. Because the contracts require a specific stage, the probability is a product of stage-transition probabilities and a timing test against the window. Governance approvals are scheduled around the league's board meetings, which makes approval timing discrete.
stages.distribution: Sequential Bernoulli transitions with log-normal durations between stages; the final-stage timing is clustered around meeting dates.

stages.name: Information flow and reporter reliability
stages.description: The market learns about the stage through reporters and official channels with different lead times and error rates; a report that a deal is 'agreed' from a top-tier reporter has a very high completion rate while 'in talks' reports often fail. The edge is in assigning the right probability to a report given its stage and source, and in timing relative to the official announcement.
stages.distribution: Report-to-event conversion probabilities vary from about 0.1 for 'talks' to over 0.95 for 'agreed' from a tier-one source; lead times of minutes to months.

stages.name: Wording and qualifying-act mapping
stages.description: The final stage is semantic: each contract's wording defines which observable counts (announcement, signed agreement, completed approval, formal adoption). Events can occur in an unrecognised form (a leak, an agreement in principle, a conditional announcement) and fail the wording, or occur on the edge of the window in Eastern Time. The mapping from real-world events to the contract's qualifying act is a model component in itself.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given wording but uncertain because real-world events are ambiguous; mass concentrated at the boundary of the window.

talent_strength.note: Team and player talent matter here only as drivers of incentives (coach firing, retirement); there is no performance measure that directly produces a transaction or announcement, so the performance link is handled as incentive, not strength.

opponent_matchup.note: No head-to-head or opponent-specific process exists for transactions, sales or announcements; counterparty feasibility is handled in the deal pipeline and rule-check inputs, not as a matchup.

role_personnel.note: Decision-makers (owner, GM, coach, player) and their tenure or career stage.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach tendencies in tactics do not produce off-court events; coach-change hazard is a function of record and organisational stability, covered by nba.org_stability.

environment.note: Venue and weather do not drive league approvals or announcements; stadium completion is the only physical-environment contract and its timeline is project-schedule driven, listed as unresolved.

game_context_script.note: These markets have no game script; the relevant timeline is the calendar and deal stage, which sit under situational and settlement categories.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities to scale; the equivalent is the number of live negotiations or candidate trades, folded into base rates in nba.offfield_base_rate.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion of reports to events and of agreements to approvals.

distribution_variance.note: Rare-event base rates and clustered timing.

officiating_rules.note: CBA and league governance rules as the rule layer.

settlement_contract.note: Stage required, window, time zone and carve-outs per series.

nba.governance_approval_pipeline.label: Deal-stage ledger and league approval pipeline
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.mechanism: Sales, relocations and expansions pass through stages (exploration, exclusivity, definitive agreement, governance vote, closing) with stage-specific completion odds and delays.
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.rationale: A rumor-level input cannot tell whether a deal is two weeks or five months from the qualifying stage, and the contracts require specific stages; the pipeline gives P(complete by date).
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.measurement: For each live deal record stage, date entered, and the historical distribution of days to the next stage from past NBA and other major-league sales (log-normal fit per stage, shrunk to cross-league pooled values with k=3 deals); compute P(reach required stage by T) = Π P(transition) × P(duration sum <= T-t); update when a stage is entered; attach the league approval vote threshold as a feasibility gate (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the exact threshold).
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.why: Sale, stake-sale and franchise-value series require definitive agreement or approval, not rumor, and timing relative to the window is the question.

nba.reporter_reliability_score.label: Reporter and source reliability by report stage
nba.reporter_reliability_score.mechanism: Conversion probability of a report into the qualifying event depends on the reporter and the claim stage (talks, agreed in principle, finalising).
nba.reporter_reliability_score.rationale: The draft input 'transactions, trades, coaching news' is a feed, not a probability; the value is a calibration table P(event | source, stage).
nba.reporter_reliability_score.measurement: Compile reports from tier-one national reporters and team beat writers over 5 seasons, label each with stage (talks / agreed / done), compute completion rate and median lead time to the official act per source and stage with beta-binomial shrinkage k=10 reports; apply to tonight's reports with time decay half-life 7 days for 'talks'; as-of report timestamp.
nba.reporter_reliability_score.why: Prices on trade and signing events should move by the conversion rate of the specific report, which this table supplies.

nba.calendar_hazard_profile.label: Calendar hazard profile (deadlines, draft, free agency, board meetings)
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.mechanism: Event hazard varies with landmarks: trade deadline, draft week, free-agency opening, league board meetings, season start.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.rationale: A uniform hazard over the window badly misprices markets with a deadline; most transactions cluster in a few days and the remaining hazard collapses after each landmark.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.measurement: Estimate discrete-time hazard by day-of-year landmark offset from 15 seasons of transactions (trades, coach changes, retirements, signings) with kernel smoothing and a landmark dummy set; P(event in remaining window) = 1 - Π(1-h_d) with hazards conditioned on the event not having occurred; incorporate announced meeting dates as known spikes.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.why: Deadline-driven markets have a convex hazard; the probability after the trade deadline passes drops to near zero for trades.

nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.label: Qualifying-stage requirement per contract wording
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.mechanism: Each series names which stage counts; a map from wording to stage lets the model score the right stage.
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.rationale: The draft treats the wording as a text input, but the useful object is a coded stage per series and the exclusions list, so the same news can be mapped to Yes/No consistently.
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.measurement: For each series code: required stage (announce / signed definitive / approved / adopted), time zone, window end, carve-outs and multi-outcome rules; fill from rules_primary and rules_secondary of every live series (22 here), mark TITLE_ONLY where no text; test with 20 historical events whether the wording would have resolved Yes.
nba.qualifying_stage_requirement.why: Fifteen of 22 series lack sampled text and the qualifying stage differs among those with text.

nba.career_horizon_signals.label: Player career-horizon signals (age, contract years, injury, public statements)
nba.career_horizon_signals.mechanism: Retirement and next-contract markets depend on age, contract expiry, injury burden, role decline and public statements.
nba.career_horizon_signals.rationale: The draft input injury_risk_season is a season games-missed expectation, not a career-horizon hazard; retirement hazard rises with age and with specific signals such as a farewell tour announcement.
nba.career_horizon_signals.measurement: Per player: age, years remaining on contract, cumulative games missed over last two seasons, minutes trend, explicit retirement statements (coded 0/1/2 by explicitness), compute discrete hazard by age from historical retirements (e.g. age 38+ about 20-25% per year, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) and multiply by an odds factor for explicit statements; effective date constraint from rule wording.
nba.career_horizon_signals.why: KXNBARETIRE and KXNBANEXTCONTRACT are player decisions governed by horizon signals that the catalog does not capture.

nba.news.reason: An undifferentiated news feed; without stage and source reliability it cannot be turned into a probability, which the reporter reliability score supplies.

interactions.mechanism: Trade probability collapses after the deadline and spikes in the days before it, so the hazard is convex in days to deadline; feasibility constraints bind most tightly in the last week when salary-matching is tested.

interactions.mechanism: Coach-firing hazard is near zero above expectation but rises sharply once a team falls below a record-versus-expectation threshold or loses a streak; the combination of underperformance and ownership impatience acts as a trigger.

interactions.mechanism: The same news item resolves differently under different wordings: an agreement in principle satisfies an announcement market but not a definitive-agreement or approved-sale market, so one report moves the series in opposite directions.

interactions.mechanism: A retirement announcement clusters after the season ends and before free agency, so the player's age hazard is conditional on being in that period; before the season's end the hazard is lower regardless of age.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate retirement announcement timing by month for players aged 36+ and test the seasonal hazard ratio.

nonlinearities.shape: Spiked and convex around deadlines
nonlinearities.why: The probability mass of trades concentrates in the final days before a deadline and then goes to zero, so linear time decay misprices markets near the deadline.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function by stage
nonlinearities.why: Probability to complete jumps at each stage (exploration about 0.2, definitive agreement about 0.9) rather than rising smoothly with time, and timing risk is lognormal.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in report stage
nonlinearities.why: Reports at the agreed stage from tier-one sources approach 1, while talks-stage reports sit near 0.1-0.3, so credence is not linear in the intensity of the language.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic threshold in the record-vs-expectation gap
nonlinearities.why: Firing hazard is near flat for modest underperformance and rises quickly after a threshold, typically in the first third of the season or after a long losing streak.

contract.settlement_definition: No live series is filed under this archetype in the ledger and no rules text exists, so the settlement logic of a multi-leg combination is NOT_VERIFIED. By construction a parlay should settle Yes only if every leg is true; what happens when one leg is void (a player inactive, a postponed game, a protected-contract fair-price void) is unknown: the combination could void entirely, drop the leg and re-price, or resolve No. The leg wording would follow the individual leg contracts (half-point team lines, N+ player thresholds, game-level postponement within 48 hours), which are visible for single-leg series elsewhere.
variants_and_edge_cases: Void-leg treatment: single-leg player contracts settle to a fair price when the player is inactive or never takes the court, so whether a parlay containing such a leg voids, re-prices at the remaining legs, or fails is the largest settlement unknown.
Same-game versus cross-game combos: legs from different games are independent, whereas same-game legs share margin, total, minutes and injury shocks; the dependence structure differs by construction.
Leg types mix half-point lines (no push) and integer N+ player thresholds (no push), but a whole-number sportsbook-style line could create a push leg whose handling inside a parlay is unseen.
Protected player legs (first-half-exit void) add a conditional-on-survival structure that interacts with other legs through the injury event.
Payoff is the product of marginals only under independence; pricing by the market maker embeds an assumed correlation that may differ from the true one.
contract.settlement_data_source: Component leg sources: official box score and final score for each leg; a combination-level rule (void or partial) is not available.

mechanism.summary: A multi-leg combination resolves true only when all legs hold, so the probability is the joint probability of a vector of events, and the information needed is the dependence structure, not just the leg marginals. Same-game legs share latent factors: the margin (favourite covering moves the starters' minutes), the pace/total (more possessions raise all counting stats), team shooting luck (a hot night lifts all of a team's scorers together), and the injury/availability shock (one news item moves many legs). Within a team the allocation of points among players is a zero-sum split of a fixed team total, so two teammates' point overs are negatively associated at a given team score but positively associated through the team total. The joint is therefore best produced by a game-level simulation with explicit factors, not by pairwise correlations, and calibrated on historical box scores. Product-of-marginals pricing is biased: positive dependence makes joint hits more likely, negative makes them less likely, and the direction flips with leg type and team side.

stages.name: Leg marginals from their own mechanisms
stages.description: Each leg has its own generating process (a spread cover from the margin density, a total from pace and efficiency, a player stat from minutes and rates), and the joint can only be as good as these marginals. The marginals must be computed on the same information set and the same scenario weights for injuries, otherwise the dependence is applied to inconsistent inputs.
stages.distribution: Each marginal is a Bernoulli with probabilities from 0.05 to 0.95; leg probabilities combine multiplicatively under independence, which is the baseline to test against.

stages.name: Shared game-level latent factors
stages.description: Same-game legs load on a handful of common factors: the game total (pace times efficiency) moves every player's counting stats in the same direction; the margin moves starters' minutes and shot attempts together in favourites' blowouts; team-specific shooting luck lifts the team's scorers jointly. A factor model estimated on historical box scores gives the loadings by leg type and player role, and these loadings are what a simulation needs.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like factor shocks with factor correlation near zero between margin and total (about 0.0-0.1) but strongly positive between total and any player points (loadings of 0.3-0.6).

stages.name: Minutes and blowout linkage
stages.description: The favourite-cover leg and the star-over leg are tied through minutes: a blowout lets the favourite cover but removes the star's late minutes, so the pair is negatively associated for the favourite's stars and positively associated for the underdog's stars. The strength is a threshold in the spread, not a constant: it appears only when the expected margin is large enough for starters to sit, and it is stronger for older stars and for coaches who pull early.
stages.distribution: Piecewise: near zero for spreads below about 6, increasing in magnitude beyond; sign flips with team side.

stages.name: Within-team allocation and common shocks
stages.description: Given team points, individual points are a split, so overs on two teammates are negatively dependent conditional on the team total, while a single availability shock (a star ruled out) moves many legs at once and in different directions (the star's legs fail; teammates' usage legs rise). A game-level simulation that draws the injury scenario first, then team factors, then allocation preserves these dependencies.
stages.distribution: Dirichlet-multinomial-like allocation with negative within-team dependence of about -0.1 to -0.3; discrete scenario mixture for availability.

stages.name: Joint evaluation and void-leg settlement
stages.description: The final stage evaluates the joint probability from the simulation and applies the settlement rules for combos: if any leg can void (inactive player, protected exit, postponement), the payoff must be conditioned on the combination's rule, which changes the effective probability. Sampling error in the simulation and uncertainty in dependence parameters give interval estimates, not points, for the joint.
stages.distribution: Monte Carlo estimate with standard error about 0.5-1 percentage points at 10,000 draws; dependence-parameter uncertainty adds comparable error.

nba.game_factor_loadings.label: Game-level latent factor loadings by leg type
nba.game_factor_loadings.mechanism: Legs load on shared factors (pace/total, margin, team shooting luck, availability) with loadings that differ by leg type and player role.
nba.game_factor_loadings.rationale: The draft lists covariance of a single player's stats, but multi-leg dependence spans legs from different mechanisms; a factor model captures it with a manageable parameter count.
nba.game_factor_loadings.measurement: Fit a Gaussian-copula factor model on 6 seasons of game-level outcomes: observed leg indicators (spread covers, total overs, player N+ at typical thresholds) transformed to normal scores via marginal CDFs; estimate loadings with 3 factors (total, margin, team luck) per team-side and role cell (starter guard, wing, big) with ridge shrinkage; report loadings and sd across 100 bootstrap draws; as-of end of the previous game.
nba.game_factor_loadings.why: Same-game dependence cannot be estimated pair by pair given the thin sample per player; a factor structure gives usable estimates.

nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.label: Within-team scoring allocation dependence
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.mechanism: Teammates split a fixed team total, giving negative dependence between teammates' counts conditional on team points.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.rationale: Treating two teammates' overs as positively dependent through the team total omits the allocation effect that offsets it at fixed pace; the net sign depends on how much variation in the team total versus in the split drives each leg.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.measurement: For each team and pair of top-6 players, compute the correlation of player points conditional on team points (partial correlation) using 3 seasons of games, shrunk to the role-pair prior with k=40 games; combine with team total correlation to get unconditional pairwise correlations; separate regimes with/without a major teammate absence.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.why: Same-team parlay legs (two players' overs) are the most common correlated combination and the net sign is not obvious.

nba.leg_void_state.label: Leg void-state probabilities and combo payoff rule
nba.leg_void_state.mechanism: The combination's payoff depends on how a void leg (inactive player, protected early exit, postponement) is treated.
nba.leg_void_state.rationale: If one leg can void, the effective probability of Yes given not void differs from the product of the remaining legs, and the void probability itself is correlated with other legs through the injury event.
nba.leg_void_state.measurement: For each leg: P(void) = P(inactive) + P(protected early exit) + P(postponement beyond 48 hours) from the availability model; compute joint outcome probabilities for each void combination; apply the contract's rule (void whole, drop leg, or No) to compute the payoff probability; the rule is an input to be read from rules_primary when a combo series is live.
nba.leg_void_state.why: The combo's expected value changes in sign for a rule that drops a void leg versus one that fails it.

interactions.mechanism: The favourite-cover and star-over pair becomes negatively dependent only when the projected spread passes about 6-8 points, since starters sit only in lopsided games; below the threshold the two are close to independent.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation of cover and star-over indicators in spread buckets of 2 points and look for a knee.

interactions.mechanism: A single pace shock lifts the game total and every player's counting stats, so total-over with two player overs has a high joint probability beyond the product; loadings determine how much.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate with and without the pace factor and compare the joint to the product on historical games.

interactions.mechanism: When a major teammate is ruled out, allocation shifts and the previously negative dependence between two remaining teammates' overs can turn less negative because both gain usage; the sign is conditional on the injury scenario.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate partial correlations separately in games with and without the major teammate.

interactions.mechanism: The same injury news produces a void leg (player inactive) or a live leg with a minute limit; the combo rule on void legs switches the payoff structure, so the effective probability is regime-dependent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute payoff probabilities under each void rule using historical status vintages and compare.

interactions.mechanism: The correlation between margin and total is close to zero overall but positive for slow-paced underdog games and negative for fast-paced favourite runaways, so the joint is not a simple bivariate normal.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation within cells of pace and spread and test heterogeneity.

nonlinearities.shape: Hinge in spread: zero below about 6, strengthening above
nonlinearities.why: The minutes link between a cover leg and a star leg is zero until blowouts are plausible and then strengthens, so the dependence cannot be a constant correlation.

nonlinearities.shape: Tail dependence in the upper tail
nonlinearities.why: Hot-shooting nights lift all of a team's scorers at once, so joint overs have more mass in the extreme tail than a Gaussian copula with the same correlations.

nonlinearities.shape: Discrete non-Gaussian marginals
nonlinearities.why: Player counts at N+ thresholds are discrete with overdispersion; normal-score transformations must use the exact discrete CDF to avoid biasing joint probabilities.
