contract.settlement_definition: Assist ladder markets settle Yes if the named player records at least N assists (strike 7.5 means 8+) in the single named game, using the player's final recorded assists. Two variants are live: KXNBAAST (unprotected) settles to a fair price if the player is inactive or active but never takes the court, and on actual assists once he enters; KXNBAASTPROT (protected) settles to the pre-tip fair price if the player enters in the first half but not after the first half (including overtime) unless he already has the required assists, and on actual statistics if he enters only after halftime. A short postponement stays open; a game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves to fair price. Assists are an official-scorer statistic subject to later correction.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is inactive, or active but never takes the court, the market settles to a fair price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Unprotected DNP: a non-appearance is void at fair price rather than No, so the Yes probability is conditional on stepping onto the court.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game the market settles based on the player's assists recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: After one minute of play the contract is a plain count; an early injury exit lowers the realised count and settles No when the strike is missed.

rules_evidence.quote: this Contract resolves to the fair price prior to the opening tip of the game unless the player records the required number of assists
rules_evidence.establishes: Protected variant voids a first-half-only appearance unless the strike is already reached, removing the injury-exit lower tail for that case.

rules_evidence.quote: records 8+ assists in the Minnesota vs New Orleans Pro Basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike is an integer 'N+' threshold (floor_strike 7.5) on one game's assist count, so adjacent rungs are survival probabilities of a discrete count.

variants_and_edge_cases: Protected versus unprotected: the same player and threshold can be listed under both tickers with different void sets, so the probabilities of Yes conditional on settlement differ.
Inactive versus active-but-no-minutes: both void at fair price in the unprotected rule, so late scratches affect edge accounting but not the settled count.
Overtime: the protected text mentions overtime for the second-half-entry test; whether overtime assists count for the total is not stated but follows official box-score totals.
Assist credit is an official scorer judgement and is subject to post-game stat corrections that can flip a rung at the threshold.
Rungs run from 2+ to 12+ for different players; the same distribution should satisfy monotone survival across rungs.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official league box score assist totals (NBA.com), including later stat corrections.

mechanism.summary: An assist is credited when a player's pass directly leads to a made field goal by a teammate, so the count is (team made field goals while he is on court) x (share of those baskets he assisted). The first factor depends on how many minutes the player plays, how many possessions the team uses in that time, the team's shooting quality that night and its assisted share (isolation-heavy teams assist less); the second factor depends on his ball-handling role, how many other creators share the floor, and how often a pass becomes an assisted make as opposed to a missed shot, a turnover or an unassisted attack. Variation therefore comes from minutes (blowout and foul truncation), teammates' shooting luck (the largest single-game noise source), lineup composition (who finishes, who else creates) and scorer-credit judgement. The count is overdispersed with a right tail for primary creators, and the discrete threshold at 8+ amplifies small shifts in the mean, so P(N+) is far more sensitive to teammates' shooting variance than to the player's own skill noise.

stages.name: Court time of the creator
stages.description: Assists accrue only on court, so the number of possessions the lead ball handler plays is the opportunity base. Primary creators play 30-36 minutes in normal games but 24-28 when the game is decided, and leave early when injured; the unprotected contract voids only a zero-minute game and the protected one a first-half-only exit. Rest and load-management habits change the starting minutes.
stages.distribution: Mixture of normal-game, truncated-blowout and early-exit regimes; sd of minutes about 5 for starters, and a point mass at zero minutes that is voided.

stages.name: Ball-handling volume and creation role
stages.description: Per minute, assist chances are produced by time of possession, touches, pick-and-roll initiations and passes; potential assists measure the pass leading to a shot attempt. Role matters: a lead guard might average 12 potential assists per 36 minutes while a wing averages 5. The presence of a co-creator (another high-usage ball handler) divides the initiations, and a missing co-creator increases the share.
stages.distribution: Potential assists per minute is stable (cross-game sd about 25% of the mean) and approximately Poisson-overdispersed per game.

stages.name: Team scoring environment and assisted-shot share
stages.description: The pool of assistable baskets is the team's made field goals, and the fraction that are assisted varies with style (ball-movement offences about 65-70%, isolation-heavy about 50-55%), shot type (threes and rim finishes are assisted at higher rates than pull-up twos) and the opponent's scheme (switching and pressure reduce clean passing lanes). The expected number of team assisted makes in the player's minutes is the volume he draws from.
stages.distribution: Team assisted FGM per game: mean about 26, sd about 4.5; positively correlated with team field-goal percentage that night.

stages.name: Conversion by teammates on the floor
stages.description: Potential assists become assists only if the teammate makes the shot, so the on-court teammates' shooting skill and shot quality set the conversion; hot or cold shooting from teammates is the largest noise term because a creator has no control over makes. With a major finisher absent, conversion drops even if potential assists stay the same, while with a creator absent the player's potential assists rise.
stages.distribution: Binomial conversion of 10-14 potential assists at p about 0.5-0.6, with additional between-game luck in teammate shooting (sd of about 6-8 percentage points); the product is overdispersed.

stages.name: Credit, distribution and rung probability
stages.description: The official scorer awards the assist by judgement (how many dribbles, whether the pass created the shot), with arena and scorer tendencies that move totals by about half an assist on average, and post-game corrections occasionally change a count. The resulting integer count is right-skewed and the rung probabilities P(N+) follow its survival function, with fair-price voids for non-appearance in the unprotected contract.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed discrete count (negative-binomial-like), variance ratio about 1.3-1.6 for guards, with scorer-level offsets of about 0.3-0.7 assists.

environment.note: Venue and altitude are not credible direct drivers of assist counts beyond the arena-level scorer credit effect captured in nba.scorer_bias; no separate environmental input for a passing statistic is justified.

game_context_script.note: Blowouts truncate minutes; close finishes add foul-driven possessions.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed count with luck from teammates.

settlement_contract.note: Fair-price voids and the protected clause.

nba.on_court_assist_share.label: On-court assist share of team assisted field goals
nba.on_court_assist_share.mechanism: The fraction of the team's assisted makes credited to the player while he is on the floor, which is the stable per-opportunity rate.
nba.on_court_assist_share.rationale: Potential assists and usage are indirect; the on-court assist share is the direct outcome rate, decomposed by lineup and whether co-creators are present, and is the cleanest basis for projecting the count from team assisted makes.
nba.on_court_assist_share.measurement: Share = player AST / (team assisted FGM while player on court), computed over last 60 games with half-life 25 games, separately for lineups with and without the top co-creator; shrink to role prior with k=300 on-court team assisted FGM; projected AST = share × expected team assisted FGM in projected minutes; as-of last game.
raw_data: play-by-play with assist credit and lineups
nba.on_court_assist_share.why: The product of share and expected team assisted makes gives the mean directly and exposes how teammates' shooting enters.

nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.label: Expected team assisted field goals in the player's minutes
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.mechanism: Team assisted makes depend on possessions, field-goal percentage, shot mix and the style-driven assisted rate.
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.rationale: The draft uses implied team totals (market-derived) as the environment; an own estimate of assisted makes depends on assisted-rate by team and by opponent coverage, which totals do not capture.
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.measurement: E[assisted FGM] = possessions(own pace composition) × FGA per possession × FG% (opponent-adjusted, 20-game half-life, k=150 FGA) × assisted rate (team assisted/FGM, opponent scheme adjustment, 20-game half-life, k=100 FGM); scale to player's projected minutes share; report mean and sd by game.
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.why: Replaces a market-derived environment with an own estimate focused on assisted makes, the quantity assists actually count.

nba.co_creator_load.label: Co-creator load (ball-dominant teammates on court)
nba.co_creator_load.mechanism: The presence of another ball-dominant creator divides initiations and assists.
nba.co_creator_load.rationale: Usage alone cannot distinguish a lone primary creator from a two-creator backcourt; assists fall when the second creator is on the floor and rise when he is out.
nba.co_creator_load.measurement: For the player and each teammate compute time of possession and touches per minute over 60 games; co-creator load = sum of the other four players' expected time of possession per minute (from lineup minutes) minus the league-average of the role; regress player's potential assists per minute on load (ridge) with team fixed effects; compute with tonight's expected lineups and scenarios.
free_sources: NBA.com tracking time of possession (via nba_api)
nba.co_creator_load.why: Directly addresses 'who else creates', the main role redistribution for assists that teammate absence alone cannot split.

nba.minutes.reason: Assists accrue per minute on court, and the minutes distribution including blowout truncation is the first factor; point projection hides the tail.

nba.pot_ast.reason: Potential assists per minute is the stable opportunity measure; it duplicates the tracking entry in content, and its tracking provenance limits free access.

nba.touches.reason: Touches and time of possession drive passes but are noisy proxies for creation; informative mainly for secondary creators.

nba.usage.reason: Usage (shot attempts and turnovers) is an offensive-load measure; for assists it is partly inversely related for creators who score, so assist share is the right measure instead.

nba.teammate_conv.reason: Conversion of potential assists into makes is the largest noise source, and regressing it to talent is correct; needs lineup-conditional estimates.

nba.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Finisher versus creator absence has opposite effects; the single with/without delta is only useful if split into creation share and conversion.

nba.opp_ast_allowed.reason: Opponent assisted-FG allowed by role is a direct pass-lane measure; small sample per role limits precision.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Switching and blitz change passing lanes but evidence is weak; effect already partly inside opponent assists allowed.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions scale chances, but only in proportion to time on ball in transition; effect is role-dependent.

nba.implied_team_totals.reason: Derived from sportsbook spread and total; replace with an own-model assisted-FGM environment and keep this as a benchmark.

nba.garbage.reason: Blowout minutes loss for lead ball handlers cuts the upper rungs; must use own-model spread to avoid circularity.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Back-to-back effects work mainly through minutes and rest decisions; small direct effect on assist rate.

nba.scorer_bias.reason: Arena scorer credit varies by about half an assist, a real but small offset useful only after other factors.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Own and teammates' status determines minutes, creators and finishers on court; vintage relative to the quote is crucial.

nba.stat_dist.reason: The overdispersed count distribution converts mean into rung probabilities; must be fitted per role, not pooled.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Post-game corrections matter only for labels near the strike; no pregame effect.

nba.tracking.reason: Described as a data source (speed, defender distance); its assist-relevant content is potential assists and time of possession already counted in pot_ast and touches.

nba.player_role_position.reason: Role classification determines the prior for pass share and who steps up when teammates are out, but is categorical and coarse.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Close games add intentional-foul possessions that mostly affect free throws; effect on assists is weak.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the assist ladder; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the assist ladder; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook assist lines are a prior on the mean; they are market prices and serve as a comparison only.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung monotonicity of the assist ladder is derived from Kalshi prices, so it flags stale quotes (an execution diagnostic) and carries no information about the underlying result.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Realised frequency by rung for the assist ladder is a calibration label set rather than a driver; thin samples per rung limit its use.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Price-bucket miscalibration for the assist ladder is measured on Kalshi prices, so it is a market-derived correction layer applied after a probability exists, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume/open interest for the assist ladder measures liquidity and attention; market-derived and not a driver of the outcome, usable only to discount thin quotes.

m.trade_tape.reason: Trade prints for the assist ladder are market microstructure; informed-flow inference from them is speculative and cannot be a causal input.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled value and timestamp for the assist ladder are labels for calibration and need reconciling against the named source; not a pregame input.

interactions.mechanism: A missing finisher cuts conversion while potential assists stay constant, a missing creator raises the player's potential assists, so the direction of the absence effect on assists depends on the absent player's role; a single dummy averages opposite effects to zero.
interactions.how_to_test: Split absence games by absent-player role and regress assists on potential assists and teammate shooting separately.

interactions.mechanism: A lead guard on a heavy favourite loses late minutes, which removes the upper rungs; effect appears beyond a spread threshold near 8-10 and concentrates in the 9+ assist rungs.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare P(9+ assists) in spread buckets for guards controlling for per-minute rate.

interactions.mechanism: Potential assists per minute scale with the share of initiations the player owns, so doubling co-creator load roughly halves his share; the effect is multiplicative on the per-minute rate and larger for players who rely on on-ball time.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress log potential assists per minute on log co-creator load with player fixed effects.

interactions.mechanism: Switch-heavy defences reduce assisted baskets for pick-and-roll creators more than for off-ball movers, so the opponent effect depends on the creator's primary action; ranking by raw assists allowed hides that.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact opponent coverage with the player's pick-and-roll initiation share.

interactions.mechanism: Teammate shooting luck is common to all of a creator's potential assists in the game, so assists have a variance larger than a binomial with independent makes; this variance is shared with teammates' scoring props.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare residual variance of assists with a binomial benchmark and correlate residuals with team three-point percentage.

nonlinearities.shape: Hinge near a 9-point spread, concave after
nonlinearities.why: Minutes for lead ball handlers fall steeply once starters are expected to sit; extra spread beyond about 14 changes little since the starters are already out.

nonlinearities.shape: Regression toward talent with a shrinkage weight near 0.6-0.7 for a 10-game sample
nonlinearities.why: Hot team shooting of the last 10 games overstates conversion; the response of future assists to recent conversion is much flatter than one.

nonlinearities.shape: Right-skewed overdispersed with heavier tail for primary creators
nonlinearities.why: A guard with a mean of 7.5 has more mass at 12+ than a Poisson, so high rungs are less steeply priced than a simple model implies.

nonlinearities.shape: Diminishing conversion at high potential-assist counts
nonlinearities.why: When the number of potential assists is very high the marginal pass is lower quality, so assists rise less than proportionally in games with extreme potential assists.

contract.settlement_definition: The live series under this key are player-status contracts with different clocks, not a game-by-game 'is he active' market. KXNBASTARTERS settles Yes only if the named player starts his team's first 2026-27 regular-season game and is on the floor at the opening tip (an announced starter who does not actually start resolves No, and later retirement or trade is irrelevant if he started). KXNBANEXTTEAM settles on the team a player is next signed to or remains with by the stated date, with Retires / No Team as a catch-all and re-signs or extensions not triggering early resolution. KXNBAONE3PT settles Yes if the player makes at least one regular-season three (Cup games before the final count; preseason, playoffs, play-in, All-Star and the Cup final do not). The sampled text covers 3 of 7 series; the rest are TITLE_ONLY.

rules_evidence.quote: must start the first regular season game for Minnesota and be on the floor at the time of the opening tip-off
rules_evidence.establishes: The starter market is one specific game with a strict physical test (on the floor at opening tip), so an announced starter who is scratched at the last minute resolves No, not void.

rules_evidence.quote: Only a made three-pointer in regular season games count.
rules_evidence.establishes: The event is a season-accumulated rare make limited to regular-season games; the exclusion list defines the exposure window.

rules_evidence.quote: NBA Cup games before the Championship game are part of the regular season and do count.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cup group and knockout games before the final add exposure, but the Cup final does not, so the exposure count is not simply 82.

rules_evidence.quote: is a free agent, whether restricted or unrestricted, for any period of time and signs a contract with any team
rules_evidence.establishes: Next-team Yes is triggered by a signing after any free-agent spell, including with the previous team, making re-signing a distinct outcome from remaining under contract.

variants_and_edge_cases: Clock mismatch within the key: first-game starter (a single decision at opening night), next team (a multi-month transaction process), one three (a season-long accrual) and return (a recovery timeline) are different processes sharing one label.
Announced versus actual: the starter market resolves No if an announced starter does not take the floor at the tip, so confirmation 30 minutes before tip still leaves a small residual risk.
Exposure window for the three-pointer market excludes the playoffs and the Cup final, so a player who only gets rare minutes late in the season has less exposure than games played.
Next-team markets contain a catch-all outcome (Retires / No Team) and re-sign handling that differ from a simple team-selection market; mutually exclusive outcomes must sum to one.
Four of the seven live series (return, play together, compete, next team conference) have no sampled rules text, so their definitions of 'return' or 'play together' are not visible.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official starting lineup and box score for the starter market, official transaction records for next team, official box scores filtered by season type for the three-point market.

mechanism.summary: These markets ask whether a player will be present in a particular role or state, and the underlying mechanisms are of four kinds. First-game starter: a coach's discrete choice among a roster after training camp, constrained by health, a minutes plan and the team's lineup philosophy; the info arrives in preseason lineups, camp reports and a pre-tip confirmation. Next team: a multi-stage transaction (contract status, cap feasibility, destination choice, trade partner assets) with a destination distribution and a catch-all outcome. Season-accumulated rare make (one three): a Poisson-like accrual with rate equal to attempts per game times make probability, multiplied by games available, so the probability is 1 - exp(-lambda x games) and is dominated by how many attempts a non-shooter takes and whether he plays. Return and play-together markets: an injury recovery time-to-event and the overlap of two players' availability, which is positively correlated with team rest decisions. Across all kinds the common ingredients are the injury status timeline, role decisions and exposure windows, and the sharp tails come from discrete decisions, not smooth rates.

stages.name: Health state and recovery timeline
stages.description: Every variant begins with whether the player is healthy: a return market is a time-to-event on recovery with a published timeline and uncertainty, a starter or one-three market requires him to be healthy for the opener or for enough games. Reported timelines are lower bounds more often than expected, setbacks occur in a fraction of cases, and restrictions after return reduce minutes. The hazard of recovery depends on the injury type and on the team's disclosure style.
stages.distribution: Time-to-event with Weibull-like shape: slow start, peak near the stated timeline, long right tail from setbacks; about 20-30% of returns slip beyond the first stated date (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Coach role decision and rotation
stages.description: For the starter market the coach chooses five from the roster given health, camp performance, lineup chemistry and the game-one opponent; incumbents start unless displaced by an addition, an injury or a strategic change (small-ball, defence-first). For the rare-three market the role decision determines whether a big is encouraged to shoot threes and for how many minutes, and for play-together markets it determines whether two players share minutes.
stages.distribution: Discrete choice over the roster with strong incumbency (starters last season retain the role about 80% of the time, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); role changes cluster in the off-season.

stages.name: Roster and contract transactions
stages.description: Next-team and related markets depend on contract status, the salary-cap and apron constraints of candidate teams, and the assets a team can send; the final destination is a choice among feasible teams with the player's preferences and the acquiring team's need. Transactions arrive in bursts around the draft, free agency and the trade deadline, and extension or re-sign events can be misread as moves.
stages.distribution: Multinomial over teams plus a catch-all with a few plausible destinations; probabilities are concentrated but with a long tail of unlikely teams.

stages.name: Season-long accrual of a rare event
stages.description: For the one-three style market the number of made threes over the season is approximately Poisson with mean lambda = sum over games of (three-point attempts per game x make probability); because the rate is small the probability is near linear in exposure at first and saturates near 1. Exposure counts regular-season games played, excluding playoffs and the Cup final, so injury time and rest directly lower it. A non-shooter who adds a three in the off-season has an uncertain rate with a long tail.
stages.distribution: Poisson accrual with parameter uncertainty (a Gamma prior on lambda gives a negative-binomial count); P(at least one) = 1 - (1 + lambda/k)^(-k).

stages.name: Joint presence and wording filters
stages.description: Play-together and starter markets depend on two or more players being simultaneously present or in specified roles, which makes the events correlated through team rest and injury policy. Wording filters (first regular-season game, on the floor at the tip, regular-season games only) set which observable counts. A single injured teammate or a coach's rest decision applies to both players, so joint presence is more variable than independent presence.
stages.distribution: Joint Bernoulli with positive dependence between rest decisions; regime effects when the stated window is short.

talent_strength.note: The core question is presence and role, not performance level; talent enters only through the coach's choice (who is better) which is covered by nba.starter_probability, and has no separate strength input for these markets.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent identity matters little for season-level or opening-night presence markets; the first-game starter market could depend on opponent size but no evidence supports a measurable effect.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and travel do not drive these presence markets beyond the minor schedule fatigue effect handled in rest and load management inputs.

game_context_script.note: Game script influences minutes during a game but not whether a player starts, returns or is traded; the one-three market's blowout-minute effect is only a second-order change in exposure.

efficiency_conversion.note: Make probability on a small attempt base.

nba.return_timeline_hazard.label: Return-from-injury timeline hazard by injury type
nba.return_timeline_hazard.mechanism: The probability a player has returned by a date follows a recovery time-to-event distribution with setbacks, not a point estimate.
nba.return_timeline_hazard.rationale: Reported timelines are lower bounds with setbacks; a return-by-date market is a CDF at a date, and the shape depends on the injury (ankle sprain versus stress fracture versus surgery).
nba.return_timeline_hazard.measurement: Weibull survival fit by injury category on 10 seasons of injuries (from the first reported timeline to the first appearance), parameters shrunk to the pooled category with k=8 cases; adjust for team disclosure style via the ratio of actual to reported timeline; P(return by T) = 1 - exp(-(t/scale)^shape) with t measured from the injury date; update at each report; as-of timestamp.
raw_data: injury events with report dates and return dates
nba.return_timeline_hazard.why: The return market is a CDF of recovery time and cannot be read from a status label.

nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.label: Rare-make accrual rate (attempts per game x make probability x exposure)
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.mechanism: P(at least one make over the season) = 1 - exp(-sum over games of attempts x probability), a Poisson accrual with parameter uncertainty.
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.rationale: Non-shooters have an attempt rate that can change after an off-season shooting project; preseason attempts are the leading indicator, and the exposure window excludes playoffs and the Cup final.
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.measurement: lambda_g = 3PA per 36 (last 2 seasons with weight 0.4/0.6, preseason attempts added at weight 2.0 per game) x projected minutes/36 x p3 (player's last two seasons shrunk to the position prior 0.30 with k=40 attempts); exposure = projected games (games available x 82-game schedule excluding the Cup final); P = 1 - E[exp(-lambda_total)] under Gamma(k,theta) for lambda with k=3; update after every game with new attempts.
raw_data: three-point attempts and makes by game, preseason included, minutes
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.why: A season-long one-three market is exposed to the attempt rate of a non-shooter and the number of games, a combination absent from the current input list.

nba.opening_night_starter_signals.label: Opening-night starter signals (camp lineups, preseason starts, coach statements)
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.mechanism: The first regular-season game's starting five is predicted from the preseason starting lineups, camp reports and coach statements, with strong incumbency.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.rationale: A season-opener market has no in-season history, so the signal is the preseason; the team's preseason starters in the final two preseason games are usually the opener's starters, but not always.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.measurement: Score for each player = 0.5 x indicator of starting both of the last 2 preseason games + 0.3 x last season's start share + 0.2 x coach statement (coded 0/0.5/1); map to probability via logistic fit on 8 seasons of opener starters; set to 0 if the status is out or doubtful; combine with injury probability; as-of 24 hours before the opener and again at confirmation.
free_sources: Preseason box scores (nba_api season type Pre Season)
raw_data: preseason starter flags, coach statement coding
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.why: The market is a single decision with an info set that is preseason only; the draft's starter probability input does not specify its sources.

nba.player_move_destination_model.label: Player destination choice model with cap feasibility
nba.player_move_destination_model.mechanism: Destination is a choice among feasible teams determined by cap space or matching assets, team need, and player preference.
nba.player_move_destination_model.rationale: A multi-outcome next-team market needs a distribution over teams; relying on rumor misses cap constraints that exclude most teams.
nba.player_move_destination_model.measurement: For each candidate team compute feasibility (cap space or matching salaries within apron rules), asset fit and need (position gap, win-now vs rebuild); estimate a multinomial logit on 10 seasons of moves with these features plus player-preference flags (stated preference, agent reports); add a catch-all with probability from age and contract status; as-of nightly.
raw_data: team payroll and cap state, historical moves
nba.player_move_destination_model.why: Next-team markets are multinomial and the feasibility screen removes impossible teams before probabilities are assigned.

nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.label: Two-player co-appearance probability with rest correlation
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.mechanism: The probability that both players appear in at least one same game (or in many) is a joint availability probability with positive dependence from team rest decisions.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.rationale: Treating two players' availability as independent overstates co-appearance when rest decisions are shared and understates it when injuries are independent.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.measurement: Per game, P(both play) = pA pB + rho sqrt(pA(1-pA)pB(1-pB)) with rho estimated from 5 seasons of pair data (team rest days, load management) shrunk to a role prior; over N games P(at least one overlap) = 1 - Π(1 - P_g) with a correction for injury duration (autocorrelation across games); update after each game.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.why: Play-together markets are about the joint presence of two players, not each one alone.

contract.settlement_definition: No live series is filed under this archetype key and no rules text exists, so nothing about the payout table is verified. The archetype describes a scalar-payout contract: a single-game player count (points in 2-point bands, made threes from 0 to 10+) is mapped to a payout schedule written in rules_primary and settled by the realised count, so the economic quantity is E[payout(count)] rather than a threshold probability. Whether payouts are linear between bands, capped at an upper band, scaled to a dollar range, and how a player who does not play or exits early is paid (fair price, zero, or the lowest band) cannot be read from any sampled text and is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
variants_and_edge_cases: Band granularity differs by series: 2-point point bands versus integer made threes with a top 10+ band, so the same payout convexity can be driven by different tails.
Cap and top band: whether the highest band is open-ended and capped at a fixed payout determines whether the extreme tail matters at all.
Non-appearance: single-leg threshold contracts in other series void at fair price for inactive players, but a scalar payout could instead pay the lowest band, an opposite treatment.
Protected versus unprotected variants may exist for scalar payouts as for threshold ladders, changing the conditional distribution on early exit.
Parity: 2-point bands interact with free throws, whose odd points shift mass between adjacent bands.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box score count for the named stat after corrections; payout table from the contract text.

mechanism.summary: A scalar-payout contract pays a function g(K) of a single-game count K, so its value is the expectation of g over the whole distribution of K, and a convex g puts most of the expected value in the upper tail where data are scarce. The distribution is built from stages: whether and how long the player plays (a mixture of normal, truncated, extended and overtime games), how many attempts occur (for threes, attempts depend on role and spacing; for points, on usage and free-throw trips), and what fraction convert (a binomial with extra within-game dispersion because shooting is clustered, not independent). Then points are a composite 2 x FG2 + 3 x FG3 + FT, so a 2-point band is a statement about the sum with parity effects from free throws. The tail beyond the 90th percentile is generated by rare combinations: high minutes plus high attempts plus hot shooting, so the payout depends on the joint upper tail rather than on any single factor, and on shrinkage choices for make rates which change the tail non-linearly.

stages.name: Payout schedule operator
stages.description: The contract defines g(K) in its rules text: band edges, payout per band, a top band that may be open-ended, rounding and the treatment of non-appearance. The value of the contract is sum over K of P(K) g(K), so the schedule is a part of the model: a convex schedule up-weights the 95th-99th percentile outcomes, a capped schedule cuts the extreme tail and a floor schedule pays something for low counts. Each series has its own schedule.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the text; the information content is in how g weights the pmf (convexity, cap, void rule).

stages.name: Playing time and extreme-minutes tail
stages.description: Minutes set the number of attempts, and the right tail of minutes (38 to 44 minutes in close games or overtime) generates the largest counts. The probability of heavy minutes depends on closeness of the expected game, bench quality, foul trouble and the coach's habit with stars; overtime adds five minutes with a probability near six percent. A truncated blowout night produces the low band and can be bounded by the payout floor.
stages.distribution: Right-tailed mixture with a heavy-minute component of 10-20% for stars and a point mass near the low band for blowouts.

stages.name: Attempt volume
stages.description: Attempts are the count of opportunities: three-point attempts depend on role (catch-and-shoot share), opponent concession of threes and team pace; field-goal attempts for the points escalator depend on usage and free-throw trips. Attempt counts are overdispersed with game-to-game sd roughly 30-40% of the mean, and they covary with minutes and with team scoring environment.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like counts; attempts per minute vary by game script and by opposing scheme; correlation with minutes about 0.6-0.7.

stages.name: Make rate with within-game clustering
stages.description: Make probability per attempt is a skill parameter shrunk toward the player's long-run rate, but within a game makes cluster beyond a binomial because of shot quality sequences and defensive attention, so the count of makes is a beta-binomial with an intra-game correlation of about 0.02-0.05. Overdispersion widens both tails and increases the weight of high counts that a convex schedule rewards; shrinkage of the rate to the mean lowers the tail.
stages.distribution: Beta-binomial with rho about 0.03: variance increases about 15-30% beyond binomial for 10-attempt games (approximate, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Composite points parity and the joint tail
stages.description: For the points schedule the count is 2 FG2 + 3 FG3 + FTM, a composite whose parity and band mass depend on free throws and threes; the pmf over 2-point bands is not the same as that over single points. The expected payout is the sum over the composite pmf, and the upper tail needs the joint of minutes, attempts, make rate and free-throw trips, which is a copula problem rather than a product of marginals.
stages.distribution: Composite integer distribution with parity structure; upper tail from the joint of volume and luck.

nba.payout_schedule_operator.label: Payout schedule operator g(K) parsed from rules text
nba.payout_schedule_operator.mechanism: The contract's value is E[g(K)] where g is the payout table in the rules text, so the schedule is part of the model.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.rationale: The draft notes that tables differ by series but has no input to hold them; without an operator, expected payout cannot be computed and convexity cannot be measured.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.measurement: For each live series parse rules_primary into arrays (band_lo, band_hi, payout) and cap/void rule fields; validate that payouts are monotone and sum correctly; compute value = Σ_k P(K=k) g(k) and sensitivity d value / d mean and d value / d variance by finite differences; version the parser by rules hash; flag unparsed tables for manual review.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.why: A convex schedule shifts value into the upper tail, and the exact shape of g decides which probabilities matter.

nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.label: Probability of heavy-minutes games (38+ minutes, OT)
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.mechanism: The extreme counts come from nights with heavy minutes, whose probability depends on game closeness, depth and the coach's usage of the star.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.rationale: A single projected minutes figure hides the 10-20% of nights with 38+ minutes that produce the top bands, and nights with 20-25 minutes that produce the bottom ones.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.measurement: Per player: share of games with minutes >= 38 over the last 80 games (half-life 30), shrunk to role prior with k=15 games; condition on own-model closeness (P(|margin| < 8) from the margin model) and OT probability 0.06; produce P(minutes >= 38) and mean count in that regime = rate per minute x 40; as-of lineup status.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.why: The convex payout puts weight on heavy-minute games, so the probability of that regime is a primary driver.

nba.within_game_make_dispersion.label: Within-game make-rate dispersion (beta-binomial rho)
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.mechanism: Makes in a game are positively correlated beyond independent shots, so the count is overdispersed relative to a binomial.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.rationale: Independence understates the tail of makes, which a convex payout over-weights; the dispersion parameter is a key tail parameter.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.measurement: Estimate rho by maximum likelihood of a beta-binomial model on 5 seasons of player-game (attempts, makes) for players with at least 200 attempts; pool by shot type (three, two, free throw) and by attempt count; shrink the player-specific rho to the pooled value with k=100 games; produce the pmf of makes given attempts n and rate p.
raw_data: player-game attempts and makes by type
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.why: Directly sets the upper-tail probability for 5+ threes or 35+ points under a convex payout.

nba.points_parity_band_mass.label: Composite points pmf with parity and free-throw effect for 2-point bands
nba.points_parity_band_mass.mechanism: Points = 2 FG2 + 3 FG3 + FT; the mass of a 2-point band depends on parity coming from threes and free throws.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.rationale: Band probabilities from a smooth normal approximation ignore the lattice structure of the composite, which can misallocate up to several percentage points between adjacent bands.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.measurement: Simulate FG2, FG3, FT counts with beta-binomial dispersion and component correlations estimated on 5 seasons; tabulate P(points = k) and aggregate to band edges from the rules; verify pmf mod 2 against historical frequencies; shrink the pmf to the smoothed empirical pmf of similar-usage players with weight 0.2.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.why: A points escalator in 2-point bands is a lattice problem; parity affects band masses.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Status vintages determine participation and the payout rule for non-appearance; teammates' status shifts volume.

interactions.mechanism: The top bands are reached when a heavy-minutes game coincides with hot shooting, and since both are rare, their joint probability determines the tail; the product of marginal tail probabilities underestimates it when close games also increase attempts.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate joint tail frequencies of (minutes >= 38, makes in top decile) and compare to the product.

interactions.mechanism: The count of made threes is attempts times make rate, so the tail is convex in both; over-shrinking the make rate shrinks the tail multiplicatively while a high-attempt shooter's tail is more sensitive to the rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute tail probability sensitivity to shrinkage constant k for low versus high attempt shooters.

interactions.mechanism: Under a convex payout, expected value is more than the payout at the mean (Jensen), so overdispersion raises value and an underestimate of variance understates it; the effect is larger the steeper the schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute E[g(K)] with the fitted pmf and with the same mean but lower variance, report the difference.

interactions.mechanism: In a blowout the starter's minutes drop and the count falls to low bands; since the payout is convex, losing the upper tail costs more than the shift of the mean, and the effect appears beyond a spread threshold of about 10 points.
interactions.how_to_test: Stratify games by spread and compute realised mean payout versus the prediction using the mean only.

interactions.mechanism: Free-throw trips add odd points that move outcomes between 2-point bands; for a player with high FTA the parity of the composite matters more than for a pure jump shooter, so the band mass is conditional on FT mix.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted band masses with and without parity modelling for high-FTA players.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex payoff in the count
nonlinearities.why: A convex schedule gives exponentially more weight to the right tail, so a small change in tail probability moves expected payout far more than a change in the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Overdispersion widens both tails
nonlinearities.why: Beta-binomial clustering raises the probability of 5+ makes beyond a binomial, an effect that grows with attempts.

nonlinearities.shape: Mixture with a heavy-minutes bump
nonlinearities.why: Counts in a 40-minute game are not a stretched version of a 32-minute game but a separate regime with higher attempts and fatigue effects, so the response to minutes is piecewise.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave shrinkage in the sample size
nonlinearities.why: Weight on a player's recent make rate grows slowly with attempts (about 0.3 at 100 attempts), so the tail is sensitive to small-sample extremes.

contract.settlement_definition: No live series is filed under this archetype key and no rules text exists, so the contract is NOT_VERIFIED. By analogy with the NBA player-stat ladders that are live (assists, combos), a free-throws-made contract would settle Yes if the named player makes at least N free throws in the named game, with a half-point strike, a fair-price void for a player who is inactive or never takes the court, possible protected variants for first-half-only appearances, overtime free throws counted through the official box score, and a short postponement staying open. These analogies are inferences and none of them is verified for free throws; technical and flagrant free throws, and whether free throws in overtime count, are specific unknowns.
variants_and_edge_cases: Technical, flagrant and clear-path free throws are made by the player (or a designated shooter) and count in the box score as free throws made, but whether the contract counts them is unseen.
Overtime free throws, which concentrate in intentional-foul situations in close games, add attempts; inclusion is likely but not stated.
Void and protected variants: an inactive player or a first-half-only appearance may void at fair price, as in other player-stat series, but this is not verified.
Strike construction: 'N+' integers with a half-point floor strike would be survival probabilities of a binomial-mixture count with a mass at zero for low-volume players.
A player who makes zero attempts is a valid outcome (not void) once he plays, which creates a large mass at zero for non-shooters.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box score free-throws-made count, with later stat corrections; the substitution/play-by-play record for any protected clause.

mechanism.summary: Free throws made = free throw attempts x make probability, and the two factors have very different properties. Attempts are an event count generated by foul-drawing: trips to the line come from shooting fouls on drives and post-ups, non-shooting fouls once the opponent is in the bonus (five team fouls in the period), technicals, and intentional fouls late in close games. Each trip yields one to three attempts, so attempts are clustered, not independent. The make probability is a stable skill, around 0.75-0.85 for guards and 0.55-0.70 for many bigs, and conditional on attempts the number of makes is nearly binomial. So variance comes mostly from attempts, which depend on minutes, the player's drive and post frequency, the opponent's foul rate, the crew's whistle, the game's closeness (late-game fouling targets poor shooters and rewards the trailing team's fouls on stars), and on the bonus state. The count has a heavy right tail from close games with intentional fouls and is zero for many games for low-volume players.

stages.name: Floor time and role in the offence
stages.description: Free throws are drawn while on court and mostly while attacking the rim or posting up, so minutes and the number of such actions set exposure. A guard who attacks the rim 8 times per game and a spot-up wing with 2 rim attempts have attempt means of about 6 versus 1.5. Blowouts remove the late free-throw-rich minutes, while close games add them for the leading team's ball handlers.
stages.distribution: Mixture over minutes regimes; attempts per minute vary by role by a factor of five or more; count of trips overdispersed.

stages.name: Trip generation: shooting fouls and bonus state
stages.description: Trips arise from shooting fouls (rate per drive or rim attempt), non-shooting fouls in the bonus, offensive fouls that do not give shots, and technical or flagrant calls. The opponent's foul-committing rate, its defensive style (rim protection without fouling vs aggressive), the crew and the team-foul state of the period determine how many of the player's actions end at the line. The trip count is clustered and has a handful of possible attempt sizes (1, 2, 3).
stages.distribution: Poisson-like trip count with overdispersion; attempts per trip 2 with probabilities of 3 and 1; bonus state creates time-varying hazard within each quarter.

stages.name: Late-game fouling and intentional-foul targets
stages.description: In the last two minutes of close games the trailing team fouls to stop the clock, choosing who is fouled: poor free-throw shooters are targeted when the rule allows, and the leading team's ball handlers collect many attempts. The probability that a given player is a target depends on his free-throw percentage, his role as a ball handler and the margin and time left. This creates a right tail concentrated in close games and a hack-a-big regime for low-percentage shooters.
stages.distribution: Conditional tail: in games within 6 points with two minutes left, attempts jump by 3-6 for ball handlers; the target rate depends on a threshold in FT% below about 60%.

stages.name: Per-attempt conversion skill
stages.description: Each attempt converts with the player's free-throw skill, which has a high signal-to-noise ratio: 200 attempts pin a rate to about 3 percentage points, and rates are persistent across seasons. For young or low-volume players the career-based estimate is noisy and informative priors come from other shooting (three-point, mid-range) and pre-NBA free-throw records. Within-game, makes are close to independent, so conditional on attempts the count is binomial.
stages.distribution: Binomial given attempts with p known to within about 3-5 points; variance largest at p near 0.5.

stages.name: Count distribution and threshold
stages.description: Making N free throws requires at least N attempts, so P(FTM >= N) = sum over attempts a >= N of P(attempts = a) times Binomial tail; the zero mass for low-volume players and the heavy right tail for stars at the line make the distribution far from normal. Settlement via the official box score is unlikely to be corrected often, but the half-point strike at integer counts means adjacent rungs differ by P(FTM = k).
stages.distribution: Mixture of a negative-binomial attempt distribution with a binomial thinning; mean 4-7 and sd 3-4 for high-volume players; zero-inflated for low-volume.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and standings pressure change minutes but have no distinct effect on foul drawing per minute; any effect works through minutes already modelled.

nba.ft_trip_structure_model.label: Free-throw trip generation model (trips x attempts per trip)
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.mechanism: Attempts are the sum of trips (shooting fouls, bonus fouls, technicals, intentional fouls) times attempts per trip (1, 2, 3).
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.rationale: The draft's ft_attempts is a rate; the clustered structure of trips matters for the variance and for the survival function at N.
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.measurement: Per player: trips per 36 = shooting-foul trips (per 100 rim attempts and per 100 post touches) + bonus trips (per team-bonus minute) + other; attempts per trip distribution from his shot mix (share of 3PA fouled, and-one rate); estimate with 3 seasons of play-by-play, shrinkage k=60 trips to position prior; simulate trips with negative-binomial dispersion estimated across games.
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.why: A trip-based model gives both mean and clustering, which settle N+ strike rungs.

nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.label: Bonus-state and team-foul environment
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.mechanism: Non-shooting fouls turn into free throws once the defending team is in the bonus, so the opponent's team foul rate and bonus minutes drive attempts.
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.rationale: Opponent foul rate enters twice (shooting fouls and bonus fouls), and the draft's foul rate input does not separate the bonus effect.
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.measurement: Opponent team personal fouls per quarter, share of quarter minutes in bonus (from play-by-play), crew fouls per game; combine as bonus_minutes_expected = f(opponent foul rate, crew rate, own pace) using 3 seasons; each bonus minute adds a rate of player-specific non-shooting-foul attempts (estimated from the player's FTA in bonus vs non-bonus minutes with shrinkage k=40 minutes).
raw_data: foul events with team foul count, quarter, crew
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.why: Bonus time is a mechanical pathway that scales every ball handler's attempts.

nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.label: Intentional-foul target probability (hack-a policy and late-game ball handlers)
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.mechanism: Probability that the player is fouled intentionally in the last two minutes of a close game, as a function of FT%, role and margin.
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.rationale: Late-game attempts form the right tail; whether a player is a target depends on a threshold in FT% for bigs and on being the leading team's ball handler.
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.measurement: Per player: attempts in the last 2 minutes of games within 6 points per 100 such minutes (last 3 seasons, shrinkage k=30 minutes); logistic target model with features FT% (below 0.60 flag), ball-handler role, trailing/leading, margin; combine with own-model P(close at 2:00) to give expected additional attempts; update each season after rule changes.
raw_data: late-game foul events with margin and clock
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.why: The right tail of free throws comes from these games and is concentrated among a few players.

nba.ft_skill_posterior.label: Free-throw skill posterior (career, three-point, pre-NBA priors)
nba.ft_skill_posterior.mechanism: Make probability is a skill with informative priors for low-sample players.
nba.ft_skill_posterior.rationale: Free-throw percentage over a short sample is noisy; for rookies and low-volume players, three-point percentage and pre-NBA free-throw data improve the estimate.
nba.ft_skill_posterior.measurement: p_hat = (FTM_3y_weighted + a) / (FTA_3y_weighted + a + b), with weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 by season, prior (a, b) from a regression of FT% on 3P% (slope about 0.5 at 100 3PA, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) and pre-NBA FT% for rookies, effective prior size 80 attempts; report sd of posterior.
raw_data: career FT and 3P attempts and makes
nba.ft_skill_posterior.why: Distinguishes a 60% center from a 75% guard and gives uncertainty for new players.

nba.ft_attempts.reason: Attempt rate is the dominant factor, but the entry mixes FT% and foul rates in one input; split into trip structure and skill posterior.

interactions.mechanism: Crew whistle scales shooting-foul rates, and attempts scale with the player's rim and post volume, so the crew effect is multiplicative with exposure: a rim attacker gains more from a high-foul crew than a spot-up shooter.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact crew foul index with drives per minute and test the slope in a Poisson regression of trips.

interactions.mechanism: Hack-a policies are triggered when a player's free-throw percentage is below about 60% and the game is within a possession or two; outside that state the target probability is near zero.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the target probability by FT% bucket and margin to find the thresholds.

interactions.mechanism: The variance of makes depends on both attempts and rate: for a 60% shooter the binomial variance per attempt is larger than for an 85% shooter, so high-volume poor shooters have a wider count distribution than high-volume good shooters with the same mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare residual variance of makes across FT% terciles at the same expected attempts.

interactions.mechanism: The bonus effect applies in the minutes after the opponent reaches five team fouls in the period, so attempts depend on when in the quarter the player is on court; a player resting in late quarters misses the bonus window.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare FTA per minute in bonus versus non-bonus minutes by player and quarter.

interactions.mechanism: In a close game the last minutes produce many free throws for ball handlers, while in a blowout those minutes are played by bench players and no intentional fouls occur; the regime depends on the margin at 5:00 left.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare attempts in the last five minutes conditional on margin buckets.

nonlinearities.shape: Binomial variance p(1-p), maximal near 0.5
nonlinearities.why: The uncertainty of makes given attempts is largest for poor shooters, so the response of P(N+) to attempts differs by percentage.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in FT% near 0.60 and in margin within about 6
nonlinearities.why: Target probability is near zero above the threshold and then jumps, so linear FT% effects misprice both ends.

nonlinearities.shape: Compound (clustered) count with 1-3 attempts per trip
nonlinearities.why: Attempts arrive in pairs and triples, giving a variance higher than Poisson and a lattice that matters at specific N.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in late-game minutes
nonlinearities.why: The last five minutes of close games carry about 25-30% of a star's free throws in about 5 percent of the minutes, so total minutes understate the weight of the closing period.

contract.settlement_definition: No live series is filed under this archetype key and no rules text exists (the head-to-head threes series KXNBAH2H3PT and KXNBAH2HTEAM3PT are filed under game_moneyline_spread and were not sampled), so settlement is NOT_VERIFIED. The three target types differ: a player-versus-player head-to-head resolves on which player has more of a named stat in a game or series (with unknown tie handling and unknown treatment if one player does not play), a series stat total or average resolves on the cumulative box-score total across the games played in a series (with an unknown rule for games missed and for an average's denominator), and Summer League stats resolve on a non-NBA schedule of games. Overtime inclusion, ties and voids are CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
variants_and_edge_cases: Tie in a head-to-head: equal counts (common for low-count stats like threes) can resolve No, void, or split; with integer counts the tie probability can be 10-20%, so the tie rule changes the price materially.

One player does not play: the market may void at fair price, resolve for the player who played, or resolve No; unprotected single-leg player contracts elsewhere void at fair price, which suggests a void but is unverified.
Series total versus average: a total depends on games played and a denominator for an average depends on games played, so a player who misses games alters the two differently.
Series length is random (4 to 7 games); whether the market is defined on all games of a series or on a fixed number of games is unseen.
Summer League games have different minute rules, game length and rosters; stats may be on a different official source with different correction timing.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box scores per game (NBA.com) for regular and playoff games; the Summer League official box scores for that event.

mechanism.summary: The three variants share one structure: a comparison or accumulation of player-game counts where the quantity of interest is the distribution of a difference or a sum rather than a threshold on one count. For a head-to-head the difference X_A - X_B has a mean given by the two players' expected counts and a variance that depends on each count's variance and on their correlation, which differs by pair type: same-team players are negatively associated at fixed team output because they split the same shots, rebounds and assists, opposing players are positively associated through shared pace, and players in different games are independent. A tie is possible for integer counts and its probability depends on the discreteness. For a series, the sum runs over a random number of games (the series length is itself uncertain and depends on the team strengths), each game's minutes are inflated in the playoffs, injuries attrite exposure, and the games are not independent because opposing coaches adjust. Summer League adds unstable rosters, announced minute plans, and rookies who play a fraction of the games. So the key information is exposure (games and minutes), dependence between the two sides, and discreteness at ties.

stages.name: Exposure: games played and presence of both players
stages.description: Both players must play for a comparison to be meaningful, and in a series the number of games played by each depends on series length, injuries and rest decisions. A star out for part of a series reduces his total; the head-to-head may void or favour the player who plays. Exposure is the product of the number of games in the series (random) and the probability of availability in each game (autocorrelated through injuries).
stages.distribution: Series length P(4,5,6,7) with mean about 5.7 for evenly matched teams and 4.8 for mismatches; availability per game with persistence across games.

stages.name: Minutes and role in each game
stages.description: For each player the minutes mixture defines how many opportunities he has; in the playoffs the rotation tightens and stars play 38-42 minutes, so per-game counts inflate relative to the regular season, while in Summer League minutes are set by a plan, rookies may be capped and veterans may be rested in back-to-back games. Minutes are correlated across the two players when they are teammates in the same blowout or in opposing teams in the same game flow.
stages.distribution: Truncated normal in the playoffs (sd 3-4 minutes) versus bimodal in Summer League (limited or full minutes); correlation of minutes between the two players depends on the pair type.

stages.name: Per-minute rates and the opponent assignment
stages.description: Per-minute stat rates come from the player's usage and role, adjusted for the opponent's defence by position and, in series, by the primary defender assigned to him; the playoff matchup assignments suppress or boost a star's counts in a way not visible in regular-season splits. Across games in a series coaches adjust coverage so the effect changes over the series.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed counts around a rate that is itself shifted by matchup assignments; matchup shifts of 5-15% of the stat in a series (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Dependence between the two counts and ties
stages.description: The difference distribution depends on the correlation of the two players' counts: for opposing players it is positive through pace and through shared game script, shrinking the difference variance; for teammates it is negative at fixed team output (one player's shot is not the other's) but positive through team pace, so the net sign depends on the stat. With integer counts, ties have positive probability, 8-20% for threes and assists, and the tie rule matters.
stages.distribution: Difference of two overdispersed counts with correlation from about -0.2 (teammates, shot-based stats) to +0.3 (opponents, pace-driven stats); discrete with a mass at zero.

stages.name: Summer League and series settlement structure
stages.description: Summer League results hinge on roster churn, unannounced minute plans and game participation (top picks play two or three games, others play five), with different stats sources and game lengths. For series totals and averages the settled quantity aggregates over a random exposure, so the pmf is a compound distribution and averages involve a random denominator. Each variant has its own settlement logic and none of the current inputs is attached to the Summer League game-selection pattern.
stages.distribution: Compound distribution (random games times random per-game counts); Summer League participation is a discrete choice with strong draft-slot dependence.

nba.pair_difference_correlation.label: Pair-type correlation of player stat residuals
nba.pair_difference_correlation.mechanism: The correlation between two players' counts differs by pair type (teammates, opponents, separate games) and by stat.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.rationale: The draft says positive correlation through game script, but for teammates the allocation effect is negative; a single sign misprices the difference variance and tie mass.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.measurement: For stat s and pair type, compute the correlation of residuals (after removing player and opponent effects and minutes) over 5 seasons for pairs of similar roles; pool in role-pair cells with shrinkage k=60 games; report the correlation and the implied variance of the difference var = var_A + var_B - 2 rho sd_A sd_B; produce P(A > B), P(tie), P(B > A) via a bivariate negative-binomial.
raw_data: player-game stats with team and opponent
nba.pair_difference_correlation.why: Head-to-head price depends mostly on the difference variance and tie mass, which the correlation sets.

nba.series_player_exposure.label: Expected games and minutes exposure over a series
nba.series_player_exposure.mechanism: Series totals depend on the number of games, availability in each, and playoff minutes inflation.
nba.series_player_exposure.rationale: The draft has a series model for the number of games but no link to each player's exposure, including injuries across games and early eliminations.
nba.series_player_exposure.measurement: E[games] = Σ_k P(series length = k) × k; exposure_i = Σ_games P(player i plays game g | series length) × expected minutes_g (playoff inflation factor from role-specific ratio of playoff to regular-season minutes over 10 seasons, shrunk with k=8 players); include injury persistence (probability of playing game g+1 given absent in g about 0.6, estimated); output exposure distribution (mean, sd).
nba.series_player_exposure.why: A total or an average depends on games played, and an average has a random denominator.

nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.label: Playoff matchup assignment shift (primary defender effect)
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.mechanism: In a series the primary defenders assigned to stars shift counts relative to regular-season rates, adjusted game by game.
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.rationale: Regular-season position-based opponent allowances miss the specific defender and the series adaptation.
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.measurement: From tracking matchup data compute for each offensive player the points/assists per 100 possessions guarded by each defender (min 50 possessions) with shrinkage to the defender's overall effect (k=100 possessions); for a series use the expected share of possessions by defender from the last regular-season meeting and playoffs-to-date; shift = Σ share × (matchup rate - baseline); update after each series game with half-life 2 games.
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.why: Stars' series counts depend on who guards them, and the variance across defenders is larger than across positions.

nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.label: Summer League game selection and minutes cap pattern
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.mechanism: Participation and minutes in Summer League depend on draft slot, contract status and team plans, with top picks playing fewer games and veterans resting.
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.rationale: Summer League exposure is the main variance of its stat markets, and none of the current inputs gives the probability that a player plays a given game.
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.measurement: Per player: P(plays game g) by draft slot bucket (top 5, 6-14, 15-30, second round, undrafted, veteran) from the last 6 Summer Leagues; minutes distribution per game conditional on playing; adjust for team announcements (coded 0/0.5/1) and for back-to-back games; combine to a distribution of games played and total minutes.
raw_data: Summer League game logs with draft slot
nba.summer_league_game_selection_pattern.why: Summer League props and head-to-heads are decided by participation first.

nba.minutes.reason: Minutes in each game feed both players' counts; the distribution differs by setting (playoff vs Summer League) and needs the correlation between the two players' minutes.

nba.usage.reason: Usage is a shot-based opportunity measure; for assists or rebounds comparisons it is the wrong driver, so stat-specific opportunity measures are needed.

nba.stat_dist.reason: Per-stat count marginals are needed for the difference and sum distributions; they do not give dependence between the two players.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Both players' status is the first gate and, for a series, status over several games with persistence matters.

nba.series_model.reason: Series length distribution is necessary for totals and averages; labelled secondary but it sets exposure and so is primary for series variants.

nba.playoff_rotation.reason: Playoff minute inflation and rotation tightening is a real effect, applying only to the series variant.

nba.summer_league_minutes.reason: Minute plans are central for Summer League but are announced late; the game-selection pattern is a separate factor.

nba.opp_def_pos.reason: Position-based opponent allowances are coarse and unstable; in series, the assigned defender matters more than the position.

nba.pace.reason: Shared pace correlates opposing players' counts, which narrows the difference variance; the effect size is modest.

nba.garbage.reason: Blowouts cut both stars' minutes in opposing pairs, increasing their correlation; applies to teammates differently.

nba.late_game_script.reason: Intentional-foul effects matter for free-throw-related stats only; weak for most compared stats.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price path for the player head-to-head and series stat markets; useful to see when information was absorbed and for calibration labels, but it is an observation of the market, never an explanatory driver of the outcome.

m.rules_text.reason: Versioned rules text defines the settled quantity for the player head-to-head and series stat markets; wording changes between series are the only way to know the target variable, so it is a required contract input, not a feature.

interactions.mechanism: The variance of a difference is var_A + var_B minus twice the covariance, so a positive correlation between opposing players narrows the distribution and raises tie probability, while a negative correlation between teammates widens it; the pair type reverses the effect of the same marginals.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation by pair type and test calibration of P(tie) and P(A>B) on held-out pairs.

interactions.mechanism: A series total is a sum over a random number of games, so a longer series disproportionately raises the upper tail; mean games enter linearly but sd of the total depends on the variance of game counts, which is larger for even matchups than for mismatches.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate series totals under different series length distributions and compare the upper-quantile differences.

interactions.mechanism: If a star is lost for the rest of a series his total stops accumulating and the head-to-head may void; the probability of staying healthy across games declines multiplicatively with persistence, creating a threshold-like drop in total after the first injury.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a model of games played given injury status after game 1 and compare series totals with and without an injury.

interactions.mechanism: The position-based allowance matters only if the assigned defender follows the position; when a coach assigns a wing stopper to a guard the position average is wrong, so the assignment overrides it.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predictions using position allowance versus assigned-defender allowance on past series.

interactions.mechanism: A top pick plays a fraction of Summer League games with capped minutes, while a veteran plays all games with full minutes, so stat accumulation is a regime-dependent mixture that depends on the draft-slot bucket.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare per-game minutes and games played across draft-slot buckets for the last six Summer Leagues.

nonlinearities.shape: Discrete, right-skewed series length (4 to 7)
nonlinearities.why: The number of games has a lattice distribution that is bimodal for mismatches and concentrated at 6-7 for even teams, so linearising by an expected length misprices totals.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating minutes inflation near 40
nonlinearities.why: Playoff minutes for stars rise from about 35 to about 40 and cannot rise further, so the inflation factor saturates with role intensity.

nonlinearities.shape: Lattice with a tie mass at zero difference
nonlinearities.why: For low counts (threes, assists) the difference has a notable mass exactly at zero (about 8-20%), so a continuous approximation underprices ties.

nonlinearities.shape: Bimodal minutes (capped versus full)
nonlinearities.why: Summer League minutes cluster at a cap for rookies and at a high value for veterans, so mean minutes are rarely observed.
